notes: 1.9-inch ST7789V 170x320 LCD on an 8-bit parallel bus (fast), backlight and power-enable pins use GPIOs. Two user buttons (BOOT/GPIO0 and GPIO14); battery voltage on GPIO4.

Variants: with/without soldered header pins, with capacitive touch panel (different pin map) and with a plastic shell. JST-GH 1.25 mm 2-pin LiPo connector and JST-SH 1.0 mm 4-pin Qwiic/STEMMA QT port.
Native USB only (no UART bridge): hold BOOT while plugging in if upload fails. GPIO count and board size are approximate (header pins are 2.54 mm; most GPIOs are used by the display).

boards.name: LILYGO T-Beam V1.2 (ESP32, LoRa, GPS)
boards.description: All-in-one Meshtastic/tracker board: ESP32 (4 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM), SX1262/SX1276 LoRa, u-blox GPS, AXP2101 power management and an 18650 holder, with USB-C, for about $31.
notes: Region-specific LoRa module: SX1262 or SX1276/SX1278 at 433/868/915/923 MHz; GNSS is a u-blox NEO-6M/M8N-class module with an RTC crystal and ceramic antenna. Always connect the LoRa antenna before transmitting.
Revisions differ: V1.1 uses an AXP192 PMU, V1.2 an AXP2101 (firmware must match). CH9102 USB-UART needs the CH343 driver on some OSes. 18650 cell is not included.
Most GPIOs are consumed by LoRa, GNSS, OLED, PMU and the button (see LILYGO pin map); only about a dozen are free on the header, so the GPIO count and board size are approximate.
A newer T-Beam Supreme (ESP32-S3, SX1262, L76K GNSS, BME280/IMU) exists if you want the S3.

boards.name: M5Stack AtomS3
boards.description: 24 x 24 mm ESP32-S3FN8 cube with a 0.85-inch 128x128 IPS screen, MPU6886 IMU, IR LED, button and Grove port; a tiny USB-C display/IMU node, now end-of-life (successor AtomS3R).
notes: End-of-life per M5Stack, which recommends the AtomS3R (ESP32-S3-PICO-1-N8R8 with 8 MB PSRAM) as the replacement; AtomS3 Lite (no screen) is a cheaper sibling.
Exposes the HY2.0-4P Grove port plus a few GPIOs (G5-G8, G38, G39) on the bottom pins; GPIO count is approximate. Built-in 5 V to 3.3 V DC-DC. Native USB only (no UART bridge).
Peripheral limits assume only the exposed GPIOs (ADC1/touch pins G1, G2, G5-G8).

boards.name: M5Stack ATOM Lite
boards.description: 24 x 24 mm ESP32-PICO-D4 (4 MB flash) cube with USB-C, SK6812 RGB LED, button, IR LED and Grove port for $7.50; a tiny, ready-to-use ESP32 with a case.
notes: Exposed pins: G19, G21, G22, G23, G25, G33 on the bottom header plus Grove G26/G32 (hence ADC 4, touch 2, DAC on G25/G26). Other GPIOs go to the button (G39), SK6812 LED (G27) and IR LED (G12).
ESP32-PICO-D4 has Wi-Fi + Bluetooth Classic/BLE and 4 MB in-package flash; USB-UART bridge on USB-C. Needs 5 V / 500 mA.
Sibling boards: Atom Matrix (5x5 LED + IMU), Atom Echo (speaker/mic), AtomS3 (S3).

boards.name: RAKwireless WisBlock Starter Kit (RAK4631 + RAK19007)
boards.description: Modular LoRa node: RAK4631 core (nRF52840 + SX1262) on the RAK19007 base with USB-C, LiPo/solar charging and sensor/display slots; BLE 5 plus LoRaWAN for about $25 with antennas.
notes: RAK4631 core module: nRF52840 (64 MHz Cortex-M4F, 1 MB flash, 256 KB RAM), SX1262 LoRa (region-specific: EU868, US915, AU915, KR920, AS923, IN865, RU864) and BLE 5; plugs into a WisBlock Base via a 40-pin connector.
The base (RAK19007) adds USB-C, LiPo charger with solar input, and slots for RAK sensor/display/GPS modules. Needs a LoRa and a BLE antenna connected before use.
Two firmware flavours: Arduino/Meshtastic BSP (RAK4631) and RUI3 AT-command (RAK4631-R). Adafruit UF2 bootloader.
GPIO count and board size are approximate and depend on the chosen base and IO modules; price is for the kit (base + core + antennas + cable).

boards.name: BBC micro:bit V2
boards.description: Classroom board with nRF52833 (BLE 5.1), 5x5 LED matrix, accelerometer/compass, microphone, speaker, touch logo and an edge connector, programmed by USB drag-and-drop.
notes: A KL27Z interface chip provides DAPLink drag-and-drop programming and USB serial; the nRF52833's own USB is not wired out.

Edge connector has 25 pads: 3 large rings (P0-P2) plus 3V and GND, and 1.27 mm pitch small pads; 19 GPIO are available but several are shared with the LED matrix and buttons (P3, P4, P6, P7, P10 and P5, P11).
On board: LSM303AGR accelerometer/magnetometer, MEMS microphone, speaker, capacitive touch logo, 5x5 LED matrix, 2 buttons and a 2-pin JST battery connector.
Programmed with MakeCode, MicroPython and Rust (CircuitPython/Arduino via community ports); I/O is 3.3 V.

boards.name: Pimoroni Tiny 2040
boards.description: Postage-stamp (23x18 mm) RP2040 with USB-C, 8 MB flash (2 MB option), RGB LED and castellated pads for soldering into wearables and small builds.
notes: Only 12 pads: 8 GPIO (GP0-GP7) plus 4 ADC-capable (GP26-GP29), 3V3, GND, VBUS.
RGB LED is active-low; BOOT switch on GP23 doubles as a user button.
Sold as 8 MB (about $10), 8 MB with pre-soldered headers, or 2 MB (about $9); frequently out of stock - Tiny 2350 is the successor.
Input 3-5.5 V, 3V3 regulator limited to about 300 mA.

boards.name: Pimoroni Tiny 2350
boards.description: Postage-stamp (23x18 mm) RP2350A with 4 MB flash, USB-C, RGB LED, Qw/ST (Qwiic/STEMMA QT) connector and castellated pads for $9.
notes: 12 IO pads including 4 ADC channels; the Qw/ST I2C connector uses GP12/GP13; BOOT button doubles as a user switch on GP23.
Also sold with pre-soldered headers (about $13); 3V3 regulator limited to about 300 mA; input 3-5.5 V.
Early boards use RP2350 A2 silicon with erratum E9 (add external pull-downs of 8.2 kOhm or less for pulled-low inputs).

boards.name: Pimoroni Pico Plus 2
boards.description: Pico-shaped RP2350B board with 16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM, USB-C, Qw/ST and SP/CE connectors and labelled pins; a drop-in Pico 2 upgrade for memory-hungry projects.
notes: Same 40-pin Pico footprint and pinout (GP0-22, GP26-28 plus ADC pins via 1 kOhm to GP40-42); SP/CE connector adds GP32-GP36; Qw/ST uses GP4/GP5.
RP2350B (QFN-80) with 8 MB PSRAM (CS on GP47); BOOT button on GP45 is usable as a user input; VSYS sense on GP43.
Stock uses RP2350 A2 silicon with erratum E9 - add external pull-downs of 8.2 kOhm or less for inputs pulled low.
A WiFi/BLE variant, Pico Plus 2 W, adds a Raspberry Pi RM2 radio. Often out of stock.

boards.name: Teensy 4.0
boards.description: 600 MHz Cortex-M7 (i.MX RT1062) in a 36x18 mm breadboard module with 2 MB flash, 1 MB RAM, USB 2.0 device+host pads, 3 CAN and 7 UARTs.
notes: Only 24 of the 40 I/O pins are on the breadboard headers (D0-D23); D24-D39, USB host D+/D-, VBAT, On/Off and Program are small underside pads. Headers are not pre-soldered.
3.3 V I/O only (not 5 V tolerant); 3.3 V regulator limited to 250 mA; USB micro-B.
Programmed with Teensyduino and a HalfKay bootloader (press the button); CAN and USB host need external transceivers/connectors.
No Ethernet PHY or SD socket - see Teensy 4.1.

boards.name: Teensy 4.1
boards.description: 600 MHz Cortex-M7 module with 8 MB flash, 10/100 Ethernet PHY, microSD socket, USB host header, 3 CAN and 55 I/O, with PSRAM/flash footprints for expansion.
notes: 42 of the 55 I/O pins are on the breadboard headers; the rest are underside pads. Headers are not pre-soldered.
Ethernet needs a 5-pin header to a magjack/RJ45 breakout (PHY is on board); a version without the Ethernet chip (TEENSY41_NE) is cheaper; lockable versions exist for secure boot.
Two unpopulated footprints on the underside for PSRAM and/or extra QSPI flash chips (solder your own); USB host on a 5-pin header.
3.3 V I/O only (not 5 V tolerant); programmed via Teensyduino/HalfKay; SparkFun now manufactures PJRC's boards.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico
boards.description: The $4 classic: RP2040 on a breadboard-friendly castellated stick with 2 MB flash and drag-and-drop UF2 programming.
notes: Micro-USB; the Pico 2 / third-party clones have USB-C.
ADC3 is wired to VSYS/3, so only ADC0-2 are free.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico W
boards.description: Pico plus an Infineon CYW43439 for 2.4 GHz WiFi 4 and Bluetooth 5.2: the cheapest wireless RP2040 board, same castellated stick and UF2 workflow.
notes: The WiFi/BT chip uses GPIO23/24/25/29 internally and the user LED hangs off the radio (WL_GPIO0), so blinking it needs the CYW43 driver.
Micro-USB; the Pico 2 / third-party clones have USB-C.
ADC3 is wired to VSYS/3, so only ADC0-2 are free. WiFi activity can disturb ADC readings on GP29/VSYS.
Also sold as Pico WH with pre-soldered headers (about $1 more).

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2
boards.description: $5 RP2350 successor to the Pico: dual Cortex-M33 or Hazard3 RISC-V at 150 MHz, 520 KB SRAM and 4 MB flash in the same breadboard-friendly castellated format.
notes: Pin-compatible with Pico 1; the RP2350A on board exposes 26 GPIO (GP0-22, GP26-28) and 3 usable ADC channels (ADC3 senses VSYS).
Boards built with RP2350 A2 silicon have erratum E9 (internal pull-downs can leave inputs high; use external pull-downs of 8.2 kOhm or less); the A4 stepping fixes it - check the chip marking.
Micro-USB; Pico 2 W adds WiFi/Bluetooth, Pimoroni Pico Plus 2 adds PSRAM and 16 MB flash.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
boards.description: Pico 2 plus a CYW43439 for 2.4 GHz WiFi 4 and Bluetooth 5.2: RP2350 power with wireless for $7 in the standard Pico footprint.
notes: The radio uses GPIO23/24/25/29 internally and the user LED is on the radio chip (WL_GPIO0), so it needs the CYW43 driver.
ADC3 is wired to VSYS/3, so only ADC0-2 are free. Boards with RP2350 A2 silicon have erratum E9 (add 8.2 kOhm or smaller external pull-downs); A4 fixes it.
Micro-USB. Also sold as Pico 2 WH with pre-soldered headers.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO SAMD21
boards.description: The original XIAO: SAMD21G18 (48 MHz Cortex-M0+) on a 21 x 17.8 mm USB-C board with a true DAC output and Arduino/CircuitPython support.
notes: 256 KB flash / 32 KB RAM; no LiPo charger and no external flash.
A0 (D0) is the 10-bit DAC output; all 11 pads are analog-capable.
SWD/reset pads on the underside for a debugger.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO RP2040
boards.description: Thumb-sized RP2040 with 2 MB flash, USB-C and an RGB LED for under $4: the cheapest way to get PIO and dual Cortex-M0+ in the XIAO footprint.
notes: Only 11 GPIO on the pads; D0-D3 are the four ADC inputs.
No LiPo charger; BOOT button for UF2 mode.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO RP2350
boards.description: RP2350 (dual Cortex-M33 / Hazard3) with 2 MB flash, USB-C, battery management and 19 GPIO in the 21 x 17.8 mm XIAO footprint, for under $5.
notes: 19 GPIO = 11 on the side pads + 8 on small back pads (need fine soldering).
Header coordinates cover the 14 side pads only.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C3
boards.description: RISC-V ESP32-C3 with Wi-Fi 4 + BLE 5, 4 MB flash, battery charging and an external antenna in a 21 x 17.8 mm board for about $5.
notes: USB Serial/JTAG only (no USB OTG/UF2).
11 GPIO on the pads; BOOT button on GPIO9; U.FL connector with an included antenna.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3
boards.description: ESP32-S3 with 8 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM, native USB, Wi-Fi 4 + BLE 5 and battery charging in the 21 x 17.8 mm XIAO footprint.
notes: The separate XIAO ESP32S3 Sense adds an OV2640 camera, digital microphone and microSD on an expansion board.
11 GPIO on the pads (D6/D7 are the UART); BOOT and RESET buttons; U.FL antenna included.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C6
boards.description: Wi-Fi 6, BLE 5 and 802.15.4 (Thread/Zigbee/Matter) ESP32-C6 with 4 MB flash and battery charging in a XIAO board: the cheap route into Matter and Thread.
notes: USB Serial/JTAG only (no USB OTG/UF2).
Software-selectable RF switch chooses between the on-board ceramic antenna and the external U.FL antenna.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C5
boards.description: First XIAO with dual-band 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi 6: ESP32-C5 with 8 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM, BLE 5, 802.15.4 (Thread/Zigbee) and battery charging.
notes: JTAG, battery-voltage and reset/boot pads are on the back; 11 GPIO on the side pads, 5 ADC channels, 2 UART, 1 I2C, 1 SPI.
External antenna via U.FL (FPC antenna included).
Sold un-soldered ($6.90) or pre-soldered ($7.99). Very new: check library/toolchain support.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO nRF52840
boards.description: nRF52840 BLE XIAO with 1 MB internal plus 2 MB QSPI flash, USB-C, battery charger and RGB LED; standby draw under 5 uA in a 21 x 17.8 mm board.
notes: Ceramic on-board antenna only (no U.FL); NFC pins accessible on back pads; 11 GPIO on the side pads.
UF2 bootloader (double-tap reset); a larger 'Plus' version with 20 pins is a separate product.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO nRF52840 Sense
boards.description: XIAO nRF52840 plus an LSM6DS3TR-C 6-axis IMU and a PDM microphone: a tiny BLE board aimed at TinyML and motion sensing.
notes: Same pads as the XIAO nRF52840; IMU is on a dedicated I2C bus and the microphone on PDM pins, so no side pads are consumed.
Ceramic on-board antenna only; 1 MB internal + 2 MB QSPI flash.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO MG24
boards.description: Silicon Labs EFR32MG24 (78 MHz Cortex-M33) XIAO with 4 MB external flash, Matter over Thread, BLE 5.3, battery charging and 19 GPIO.
notes: A 'Sense' version (separate SKU, $10.99) adds an analog microphone and 6-axis IMU.
1536 KB internal flash plus 4 MB onboard flash; 19 GPIO = 11 side pads + 8 back pads; ceramic antenna with optional external U.FL.
The wiki documents a recovery procedure for boards that appear bricked after entering deep sleep.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO RA4M1
boards.description: Renesas RA4M1 (the Arduino UNO R4 MCU, 48 MHz Cortex-M4F) in the XIAO footprint with 14-bit ADC, 12-bit DAC, CAN controller and battery charging.
notes: 256 KB flash / 32 KB SRAM / 8 KB EEPROM; the CAN controller needs an external transceiver (none on board).
19 GPIO = 11 side pads + 8 back pads (D11-D18); 3.3 V I/O, unlike the 5 V UNO R4.
No Wi-Fi/BLE on this MCU; deep-sleep draw about 45 uA.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO nRF54L15
boards.description: Nordic nRF54L15 (128 MHz Cortex-M33 + RISC-V coprocessor) XIAO with BLE 6.0 incl. channel sounding, Thread/Zigbee/Matter, NFC, USB-C and battery charging.
notes: 16 GPIO (D0-D15): D0-D10 on the side pads, D11-D15 on the back; the Sense version (separate SKU, $15.99) adds an IMU and PDM microphone and exposes 14 GPIO.
1.5 MB NVM (RRAM) / 256 KB RAM; supported by the Nordic nRF Connect SDK (Zephyr) and PlatformIO; check Arduino core status.
Standard 14-pad XIAO footprint (7 per side, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing); header coordinates assume the pads are centred on the 21 mm board length.

boards.name: Seeed Studio Wio-E5 mini
boards.description: STM32WLE5JC LoRa module on a USB-C carrier with SMA and U.FL antenna connectors; ships with AT-command LoRaWAN firmware (EU868/US915), the easiest way into LoRaWAN.
notes: Factory AT firmware is programmed with read-protection level 1: removing it erases the flash and it cannot be restored.
PB13 doubles as the factory bootloader pin (BOOT button); PB6/PB7 (USART1) are shared with the on-board USB-UART bridge and PA13/PA14 are the SWD pins.
Module transmits only through RFO_HP (up to about +20.8 dBm); 868/915 MHz, LoRa and (G)FSK/(G)MSK/BPSK; headers come as two 1x12 strips that you solder yourself.

boards.name: SparkFun Pro Micro - RP2040
boards.description: RP2040 in the classic Pro Micro footprint with 16 MB flash, USB-C, Qwiic and a WS2812 LED; castellated, breadboard-friendly and 3.3 V logic.
notes: Same 24 pad order as an ATmega32U4 Pro Micro but 3.3 V logic: 5 V Pro Micro shields/sketches need level shifting.
Pin numbers are RP2040 GPIO numbers; GP0/GP1 = UART0, GP8/GP9 = UART1, GP20-23 = SPI, A0-A3 = ADC.
SparkFun's page counts 20 GPIO; 18 are on the 24 header pads.
Resettable PTC fuse, BOOT and RESET buttons; 16 MB QSPI flash.

boards.name: SparkFun Pro Micro - RP2350
boards.description: RP2350 in the Pro Micro footprint with 16 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM, USB-C, Qwiic and a WS2812 LED: the most memory in the classic 24-pad layout.
notes: RP2350A (30 GPIO) of which 18 are broken out on the 24 pads; 3.3 V logic.
PSRAM is on the QSPI bus (APS6404L 8 MB); PSRAM support depends on the SDK/firmware (SparkFun MicroPython build, Pico SDK with PSRAM init).
Pin numbers are RP2350 GPIO numbers; GP0/GP1 = UART0, GP8/GP9 = UART1, GP20-23 = SPI.
Resettable PTC fuse, BOOT and RESET buttons.

boards.name: SparkFun Thing Plus - RP2040
boards.description: Feather-footprint RP2040 with 16 MB flash, microSD slot, 500 mA LiPo charger with fuel gauge, Qwiic, USB-C and WS2812: a ready-made data logger platform.
notes: Feather-compatible header geometry but 58.4 mm long (extra space for the microSD socket); header pin 16 is the WS2812 data-out, positions 9-10 are unconnected.
microSD is SPI-mode on dedicated GPIO; MAX17048 fuel gauge on I2C; 2x5 1.27 mm JTAG/SWD pads.
Header labels derived from SparkFun's Eagle files; SCL/SDA are GP7/GP6 (I2C1, shared with the Qwiic connector).

boards.name: SparkFun Thing Plus Matter - MGM240P
boards.description: Silicon Labs MGM240P (EFR32MG24) Thing Plus for Matter over Thread, Zigbee and BLE 5.3 with Qwiic, microSD and LiPo charger; retired by SparkFun but a handy Matter dev board.
notes: SparkFun has retired this product (no longer sold new); the price shown is its last retail price.
MGM240P module has an integrated antenna; 1536 KB flash / 256 KB RAM; 2x5 1.27 mm SWD/PTI pads for a J-Link.
MAX17048 fuel gauge, 500 mA MCP73831 charger, microSD socket; header labels derived from SparkFun's Eagle files.

boards.name: SparkFun RedBoard Artemis Nano
boards.description: Breadboard-friendly Nano-style board on the ultra-low-power Apollo3 (Cortex-M4F with BLE 5): USB-C, Qwiic, PDM microphone, LiPo charging and 17 interrupt-capable GPIO.
notes: 3.3 V logic only; all 17 GPIO are interrupt capable; 2 UART, 4 I2C and 2 SPI instances available (SparkFun).
Programmed through the on-board USB-serial bridge with SparkFun's Arduino core; 1 MB flash / 384 KB RAM, 48 MHz (96 MHz turbo).
2x5 1.27 mm SWD/JTAG pads and a PDM microphone on the back side.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-C031C6 (Nucleo-64)
boards.description: Cheapest way into STM32C0: a 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ (32 KB flash) on a Nucleo-64 with ST-LINK/V2-1, Arduino Uno V3 headers and full ST morpho access.
notes: ST-LINK/V2-1 gives drag-and-drop flashing, a virtual COM port and SWD debug; no separate programmer needed.
STM32C031 has no USB peripheral, so the only USB port is the ST-LINK one. 32 KB flash / 12 KB RAM is fine for simple control, tight for RTOS plus protocol stacks.
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-G0B1RE (Nucleo-64)
boards.description: Nucleo-64 for the feature-rich STM32G0B1: 64 MHz Cortex-M0+, 512 KB flash, USB FS, UCPD (USB-C PD) and 2 FDCAN, with ST-LINK/V2-1 and Arduino Uno V3 headers.
notes: The MCU has 2x FDCAN, USB FS device/host and UCPD, but the board fits no CAN transceiver; add an external PHY. USB/UCPD pins are on the morpho headers - check the schematic before assuming a user USB-C connector is fitted.
ST-LINK/V2-1 gives drag-and-drop flashing, a virtual COM port and SWD debug.
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-G431KB (Nucleo-32)
boards.description: Breadboard-friendly Arduino-Nano-format Nucleo with a 170 MHz Cortex-M4F (CORDIC/FMAC, op-amps, comparators, FDCAN) and a built-in ST-LINK/V2-1.
notes: Nano pin layout (2x15, 15.24 mm row spacing) but signals differ from an Arduino Nano; IO is 3.3 V only. One user LED (LD3) and a reset button; no user button.
UFQFPN32 MCU: only 22 I/Os reach the headers (D0-D13, A0-A7). PA11/PA12 are shared between USB D-/D+ and FDCAN (D10/D2); there is no USB connector or CAN transceiver on the board.
Header pin order follows ST's Nucleo-32 pinout (CN3 = D1..D12, CN4 = D13..VIN); physical orientation was derived from the Arduino Nano layout, not measured on a board.
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-G474RE (Nucleo-64)
boards.description: The motor-control / digital-power Nucleo: 170 MHz Cortex-M4F with HRTIM, 5 ADCs, op-amps, comparators and 3 FDCAN on a Nucleo-64 with ST-LINK and Arduino Uno V3 headers.
notes: FDCAN and USB FS pins (PA11/PA12) are on the headers, but the board has no CAN transceiver and no user USB connector.
Popular for BLDC/PMSM FOC with X-NUCLEO-IHM motor-driver shields.
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-F411RE (Nucleo-64)
boards.description: Long-running Nucleo-64 classic: 100 MHz Cortex-M4F with USB OTG FS, Arduino Uno V3 + morpho headers and ST-LINK/V2-1; supported by Arduino-STM32, Mbed, Zephyr and PlatformIO.
notes: ST-LINK/V2-1 uses a Mini-B USB connector (not micro/USB-C). Its SWD header (CN4) can program other STM32 targets.
The MCU's USB OTG FS pins (PA11/PA12) are only on the headers; there is no user USB connector.
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-F446RE (Nucleo-64)
boards.description: Faster F4 Nucleo-64: 180 MHz Cortex-M4F with 2 CAN, SAI/I2S and USB OTG on the Arduino Uno V3 + morpho headers, programmed through the built-in ST-LINK/V2-1.
notes: ST-LINK/V2-1 uses a Mini-B USB connector. CAN and USB OTG pins are only on the headers; no CAN transceiver or user USB connector is fitted.
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-H743ZI2 (Nucleo-144)
boards.description: Obsolete 480 MHz Cortex-M7 Nucleo-144 with Ethernet RJ45, USB OTG and ST-LINK; ST now recommends the otherwise identical NUCLEO-H753ZI (adds crypto).
notes: Marked obsolete/NRND by ST and DigiKey (DigiKey names NUCLEO-H753ZI as the replacement; ST says a project for the ZI2 loads on the H753ZI unchanged apart from crypto). Price is the last distributor/aggregator quote and stock is only grey-market or old inventory.
STM32H743ZIT6 (LQFP144); Zio (Arduino Uno V3 superset) plus ST morpho headers; 100 GPIO is an estimate of what reaches the connectors.
The KiCad symbol is the original NUCLEO-H743ZI; the footprint is the common Nucleo-144 morpho connector footprint.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-H563ZI (Nucleo-144)
boards.description: 250 MHz Cortex-M33 (TrustZone) Nucleo-144 with Ethernet, USB-C, FDCAN, 2 MB flash and ST-LINK; a modern secure, connected alternative to the older H7 boards.
notes: Zio (Arduino Uno V3 superset) plus ST morpho headers; ST-LINK uses a micro-USB port and the user USB port is a separate connector (dual USB). 100 GPIO is an estimate of what reaches the connectors.
ST eStore list price jumped well above the original launch price; check current stock and price, as DigiKey showed long lead times.
KiCad footprint is the common Nucleo-144 morpho connector footprint (no dedicated symbol for this board).

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-H723ZG (Nucleo-144)
boards.description: Fastest Nucleo-144 in this set: 550 MHz Cortex-M7 with 1 MB flash, Ethernet RJ45, USB OTG and ST-LINK, plus Arduino Uno V3 and morpho headers.
notes: STM32H723 has a USB OTG HS controller that needs an external ULPI PHY for 480 Mbit/s; the board's user USB port runs full-speed. 100 GPIO is an estimate of what reaches the connectors.
KiCad footprint is the common Nucleo-144 morpho connector footprint (no dedicated symbol for this board).
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-L432KC (Nucleo-32)
boards.description: Ultra-low-power Arduino-Nano-format Nucleo: 80 MHz Cortex-M4F with crystal-less USB FS, CAN and 256 KB flash, plus a built-in ST-LINK/V2-1.
notes: Nano pin layout (2x15, 15.24 mm row spacing) but signals differ from an Arduino Nano; IO is 3.3 V only. One user LED (LD3, shared with D13/PB3) and a reset button; no user button.
USB FS (PA11/PA12 = D10/D2) and CAN pins are on the headers only; no USB connector or CAN transceiver is fitted.
Header pin order follows ST's Nucleo-32 pinout (CN3 = D1..D12, CN4 = D13..VIN); physical orientation was derived from the Arduino Nano layout, not measured on a board.
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-U575ZI-Q (Nucleo-144)
boards.description: Low-power Cortex-M33 (160 MHz, TrustZone, 2 MB flash, on-chip SMPS) Nucleo-144 with USB-C, Arduino Uno V3 and morpho headers and ST-LINK; good for secure battery designs.
notes: The -Q suffix means the SMPS-equipped STM32U575ZIT6Q. The U575 has no Ethernet MAC, so unlike the H5/H7 Nucleo-144 boards there is no RJ45.
ST-LINK uses a micro-USB port and the user USB port is a separate connector. 100 GPIO is an estimate of what reaches the connectors.
KiCad footprint is the common Nucleo-144 morpho connector footprint (no dedicated symbol for this board).
Price is the ST eStore list price seen in late 2026 (US tariff-era pricing); older articles quote lower numbers, so re-check before ordering.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-WB55RG (Nucleo-64)
boards.description: Easiest way into STM32WB: Bluetooth 5 LE and 802.15.4 (Zigbee/Thread) dual-core Cortex-M4/M0+ on a Nucleo-64 with USB FS, PCB antenna, ST-LINK and Arduino headers.
notes: The wireless stack runs on the Cortex-M0+ radio core and must be loaded once as a binary through the FUS using STM32CubeProgrammer.
Has a second USB connector for the MCU's USB FS device port in addition to the ST-LINK port. Also sold with a USB dongle as P-NUCLEO-WB55.
ST eStore price was far above the original launch price in late 2026 (Arrow showed about $34); compare distributors.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-WBA55CG (Nucleo-64)
boards.description: Newest STM32 wireless Nucleo-64: Cortex-M33 with TrustZone, Bluetooth 5.4 LE and 802.15.4 (Thread/Zigbee/Matter), PCB antenna and ST-LINK; the successor to the WB55 for new designs.
notes: Single-core Cortex-M33 runs both the application and the radio stack (unlike the dual-core WB55). 38 GPIO is an estimate for the UFQFPN48 part.
ST eStore price is high; Future, Arrow and Avnet listed about $58-61 in late 2026.
USB connector type for the ST-LINK port was not verified against the user manual.

boards.name: ST NUCLEO-WL55JC1 (Nucleo-64, 868/915 MHz)
boards.description: LoRa / (G)FSK sub-GHz dual-core (Cortex-M4 + M0+) Nucleo-64 with SMA antenna, ST-LINK and Arduino headers; the JC1 is the 868/915 MHz (EU/US/AU) version.
notes: Order code matters: NUCLEO-WL55JC1 is tuned for about 865-930 MHz (EU868/US915); NUCLEO-WL55JC2 (about $42.5) is the low-band 433/470-510 MHz board and is not interchangeable.
The LoRa radio is the MCU's built-in sub-GHz transceiver (no extra radio chip). RF switch and TCXO use a few pins, so about 40 GPIO are free (estimate).
The product page and id cover both JC1 and JC2; data here is for the JC1.

boards.name: nRF52840 DK (PCA10056)
boards.description: The reference Bluetooth LE / Thread / Zigbee board for the nRF52840: on-board J-Link OB debugger, Arduino Uno R3 headers, 1 MB flash plus 8 MB QSPI flash, USB device and NFC antenna.
notes: Two micro-USB ports: one for the J-Link OB debugger (with virtual COM port), one for the nRF52840's native USB device. Can also emulate nRF52811.
VDD defaults to 3.0 V from USB (1.7-5 V when externally powered), so IO is 3.3 V-class and not 5 V tolerant. Powered from USB, external supply, LiPo connector or CR2032 holder.

Includes an NFC antenna and an SWF RF-measurement connector. Flash total counts 1 MB internal plus the 8 MB on-board QSPI flash. Size, GPIO count and price (DigiKey, Nordic does not list one) are approximate.

boards.name: nRF54L15 DK (PCA10156)
boards.description: Low-power Bluetooth LE / Thread / Zigbee / Matter kit: 128 MHz Cortex-M33 plus RISC-V coprocessor, J-Link OB debugger, 8 MB external flash, and it can emulate the nRF54L10 and nRF54L05.
notes: MCU has 1.5 MB non-volatile (RRAM) and 256 KB RAM; the board adds 8 MB external SPI flash (flashMB = 1.5 + 8).

Four user LEDs and four buttons, power-measurement pins, 2.4 GHz and NFC antennas plus an SWF RF connector. The Arduino Uno R3-compatible header and the USB-C connector are from memory of Nordic's hardware docs and were not confirmed on the fetched pages.
Board size and usable GPIO count are estimates.

boards.name: nRF9151 DK (PCA10171)
boards.description: Cellular IoT dev kit: LTE-M, NB-IoT, DECT NR+ and GNSS from the nRF9151 SiP, with J-Link OB debugger, Arduino Uno R3 headers, nano-SIM/eSIM footprints and preloaded SIM cards.
notes: Ships with Onomondo and Wireless Logic SIM cards preloaded with free data (promotion terms may change). Has LTE-M/NB-IoT and GNSS antennas; an SMA-connector variant (NRF9151-SMA-DK) costs about $120-165.
The radio is part of the nRF9151 SiP, so there are no extra radios. The DK's GPIO logic level is switchable (1.8 V / 3 V class); 3.3 is recorded as the closest schema value.
Includes a PCAL6408A I/O expander on I2C. Distributor price about $92-102; $99 is the Symmetry/Avnet/Newark list price. USB connector type, size and GPIO count were not verified.

boards.name: FRDM-MCXA153
boards.description: $15 FRDM board for the 96 MHz Cortex-M33 MCX A153 with an MCU-Link CMSIS-DAP debugger, USB-C, and Arduino, FRDM, Pmod and mikroBUS headers.
notes: Two USB-C ports: one for the MCU-Link debug probe, one for the MCU's full-speed USB device port. Includes an I3C/I2C temperature sensor and a USB-C cable.
128 KB flash / 32 KB RAM (8 KB with ECC). The kit supports MCXA13x/14x/15x parts. RGB LED, board size and GPIO count are approximate.

boards.name: FRDM-MCXN947
boards.description: $25 FRDM board for the dual-core Cortex-M33 MCX N947 with eIQ NPU: MCU-Link debugger, Ethernet, USB-C, CAN-FD transceiver and Arduino, FRDM, Pmod and mikroBUS headers.
notes: Dual Cortex-M33 at 150 MHz with up to 2 MB dual-bank flash. NXP lists extra FlexIO/LCD and SmartDMA/camera headers; the microSD slot comes from Zephyr docs and was not on the NXP page.
NXP's page showed 'Pending Stock'/backorder in late 2026; DigiKey and Arrow had stock. Board size and GPIO count are approximate.

boards.name: MIMXRT1060-EVKC
boards.description: Full-featured i.MX RT1062 (600 MHz Cortex-M7) evaluation board with 32 MB SDRAM, 8 MB QSPI + 64 MB HyperFlash, Ethernet, CAN, SD, audio codec, LCD/camera connectors and on-board debug probe.
notes: EVKC is the current active revision (EVKB is no longer manufactured). The NXP product page is the EVKB/EVKC combined page. MCU is MIMXRT1062DVL6B.
i.MX RT has no internal flash: code runs from the 8 MB QSPI or 64 MB HyperFlash (flashMB = 8 + 64). 256 Mb SDRAM is recorded as psramMB = 32.

Parallel LCD and camera connectors are fitted but no display or camera is included (NXP sells a 4.3-inch LCD board separately, about $45). Micro-USB host/OTG ports plus a debug USB port. Board size and GPIO count are approximate.

boards.name: LPCXpresso55S69
boards.description: Dual Cortex-M33 (150 MHz, TrustZone) LPCXpresso board with on-board Link2 CMSIS-DAP/J-Link debug probe, Arduino and mikroBUS headers, Pmod, microSD, audio codec and USB host/device.
notes: Order code LPC55S69-EVK. On-board Link2 debug probe supports CMSIS-DAP and SEGGER J-Link firmware; includes MMA8652 accelerometer, stereo audio codec with line in/out, high-speed and full-speed USB ports.

Prices vary widely (NXP $84.77 pending stock, Mouser ~$75, Newark ~$69, DigiKey ~$104); the older figure of about $50 is gone. External flash size was not verified (flashMB counts only the 640 KB internal flash). Board size and GPIO count are approximate.

boards.name: LP-MSPM0G3507 LaunchPad
boards.description: Low-cost LaunchPad for the 80 MHz Cortex-M0+ MSPM0G3507 (128 KB flash, fast 12-bit ADC, op-amp, DAC) with XDS110-class debugger, EnergyTrace and 40-pin BoosterPack headers.
notes: Has three buttons, two LEDs (one RGB), temperature and light sensors, and a buffer to show the 4 MHz ADC. Standard 40-pin BoosterPack headers, not Arduino-compatible.
TI does not show a price on the tool page; $20.56 is a university bookstore price and DigiKey listed $25.70 (backordered). Board size, GPIO count and the connector type are approximate.

boards.name: LP-MSPM0C1104 LaunchPad
boards.description: Tiny, very cheap USB-C LaunchPad for the MSPM0C1104 (24 MHz Cortex-M0+, 16 KB flash) with an on-board XDS110-class debug probe, LED, button and 20-pin BoosterPack headers.
notes: The MSPM0C1104 comes in tiny packages (the 8-pin variants have 6 GPIO, the larger VSSOP-20 up to 18); gpio = 6 is a conservative estimate for the board even though it has 20-pin BoosterPack headers.
TI list price at launch was $5.99; DigiKey and Mouser listed $7.19 (tariff note). Board size and GPIO count are estimates.

boards.name: MSP-EXP430FR2433 LaunchPad
boards.description: Classic ultra-low-power FRAM LaunchPad: MSP430FR2433 (16 MHz, 15.5 KB FRAM) with eZ-FET debugger and EnergyTrace, 20-pin BoosterPack headers and a supercapacitor footprint.
notes: Two buttons and two LEDs; supports a user-installed supercapacitor instead of a battery. Includes a micro-USB cable.
$9.99 is TI's own price as reported by an aggregator (not confirmed on TI's page); DigiKey and Mouser list about $13-14. Board size and GPIO count are approximate.

boards.name: LP-CC2652R7 LaunchPad
boards.description: Multi-protocol 2.4 GHz LaunchPad: BLE 5, Zigbee, Thread and proprietary on the CC2652R7 (Cortex-M4F, 704 KB flash) with XDS110 debugger, on-board antenna and 40-pin BoosterPack headers.
notes: The board carries the CC2652R7 (704 KB flash) rather than the older CC2652R (352 KB); mcuId points at the CC2652R family entry. Includes a micro-USB cable.
TI price is from the page's structured data. Board size and GPIO count are approximate.

boards.name: EK-TM4C123GXL (Tiva C LaunchPad)
boards.description: The long-lived Tiva C LaunchPad: 80 MHz Cortex-M4F with 256 KB flash, USB OTG, 2 CAN, 8 UARTs and an ICDI debugger on 40-pin BoosterPack headers, well documented with TivaWare.
notes: Legacy Tiva C platform: still sold but TI now steers new designs to MSPM0, CC13xx/26xx and C2000. Has two micro-USB ports (debug and device/OTG), two buttons and an RGB LED.
No price on TI's tool page; $22.35 is Arrow's price and DigiKey listed $28.78 (out of stock) in late 2026. The 2013 launch price was $12.99. Board size and GPIO count are approximate.

boards.name: EK-RA6M5
boards.description: Feature-packed RA6M5 (200 MHz Cortex-M33, TrustZone) kit with J-Link OB, Ethernet, USB FS/HS, CAN FD transceiver, 64 MB Octo-SPI and 32 MB Quad-SPI flash, and Arduino/Pmod/mikroBUS/Qwiic/Grove connectors.
notes: Order code RTK7EKA6M5S00001BE. Four 40-pin headers give native access to the 176-pin MCU. Three user LEDs (red/blue/green), two user buttons; the kit includes micro-USB cables and an Ethernet cable.

flashMB = 2 MB internal + 32 MB QSPI + 64 MB OSPI as listed by Renesas; Zephyr's page lists the QSPI as 32 MB (256 Mb), so the OSPI size is the least certain figure. $54.38 is Renesas' budgetary price; DigiKey lists about $60. Board size and GPIO count are approximate.

boards.name: FPB-RA4E2
boards.description: Cheap $11 Fast Prototyping Board for the RA4E2 (100 MHz Cortex-M33): built-in J-Link OB debugger, Arduino Uno and Pmod headers, and through-holes to every MCU pin.
notes: R7FA4E2B93CFM (LQFP-64, 128 KB flash, 40 KB RAM). Renesas lists $11.14 as a budgetary price.
USB connector type, LED/button set, board size and GPIO count were not given on Renesas' page and are estimates.

boards.name: SAM D21 Curiosity Nano (DM320119)
boards.description: Small breadboard-friendly SAMD21G17D board with a built-in nEDBG-class debugger, virtual COM port and drag-and-drop programming, plus adjustable 1.7-3.6 V target voltage.
notes: One yellow user LED and one mechanical switch; the debugger also provides a Data Gateway Interface logic analyzer. Powered from USB through a MIC5353 LDO (500 mA).
Headers are not populated by default. Microchip's own page returns 403 to automated fetches so price comes from DigiKey ($10.61); board size and GPIO count are estimates.

boards.name: SAM E51 Curiosity Nano (EV76S68A)
boards.description: Breadboard-friendly SAME51J20A (120 MHz Cortex-M4F, 1 MB flash, CAN-FD, USB) board with a built-in debugger and virtual COM port for evaluating the SAM E5x family.
notes: Price is Newark's listing ($24.99); a DigiKey bulk-packaging listing appeared at about $10 but looked inconsistent. Microchip's page was not fetchable, so features other than the SAME51J20A MCU rely on the product family.
Curiosity Nano boards are minimal: CAN-FD pins are on the headers but no CAN transceiver is fitted (add one externally). Board size and GPIO count are estimates.

boards.name: SAM E54 Xplained Pro (ATSAME54-XPRO)
boards.description: Full evaluation board for the SAME54P20A (120 MHz Cortex-M4F, 1 MB flash) with EDBG debugger, Ethernet, CAN-FD, SD card, USB and Xplained Pro extension headers.
notes: Uses Atmel Xplained Pro extension headers (EXT1-EXT3), not Arduino. Ethernet PHY, CAN transceiver, SD slot and USB host/device features are from the board family description and were not confirmed on a fetched page. Price ranges from about $84 (aggregator) to $113 (DigiKey).
flashMB counts only the 1 MB internal flash (external QSPI flash size not verified). Board size and GPIO count are estimates.

boards.name: AVR128DA48 Curiosity Nano (DM164151)
boards.description: 5 V-capable AVR128DA48 (24 MHz, 128 KB flash) on a small breadboard-friendly board with a built-in nEDBG UPDI debugger and virtual COM port; great for modern AVR work.
notes: The AVR DA itself runs from 1.8-5.5 V and has 5 V-tolerant IO, but the board's target rail is 3.3 V by default (adjustable). Programmed over UPDI by the on-board debugger; also works with Arduino (DxCore) and PlatformIO.
Microchip's page was not fetchable, so price is DigiKey's $10.61 (Mouser's older $24 listing looks stale). Board size and GPIO count are estimates.

boards.name: xG24 Explorer Kit (XG24-EK2703A)
boards.description: Compact EFR32MG24 (78 MHz Cortex-M33, 1.5 MB flash) wireless kit for BLE, Thread, Zigbee and Matter, with on-board J-Link, mikroBUS and Qwiic connectors and breakout pads.
notes: On-board SEGGER J-Link, virtual COM port and packet trace; supports Adafruit, MikroElektronika, Seeed and SparkFun add-on connectors (Qwiic). Two LEDs and two push buttons.
DigiKey lists $40.26, Symmetry $39.00, Arrow $36.18. Silicon Labs' page returns 403 to automated fetches. Board size and GPIO count are estimates.

boards.name: CH32V307V-EVT-R1
boards.description: Cheap (~$11) RISC-V4F evaluation board for the CH32V307: 144 MHz, USB HS, 10M Ethernet, 8 UARTs and on-board WCH-Link for debugging and download.
notes: The R1 version includes the WCH-Link (the older R0 does not). Sold mainly through LCSC, PCBX, AliExpress and eBay rather than a WCH store; prices run about $9-17 and LCSC is often out of stock. The CH32V307 offers up to 480 KB flash in some configurations; the MCU entry lists 256 KB.
CNX Software notes 8 UART ports; the CH32V307 has USB HS with built-in PHY and a 10M Ethernet PHY. USB connector types, size and the exact set of on-board connectors were not verified from a manual.

boards.name: HPM5300EVK
boards.description: HPMicro's evaluation board for the HPM5361 (480 MHz RISC-V): on-board FT2232 debugger, 2x20 IO expansion header, motor-control and sensor interfaces, ADC SMA input and CAN.
notes: No public price was found: HPMicro sells through distributors and Taobao; $35 is an estimate. The HPM5361 has no internal flash, so the board's external QSPI flash holds the code (8 MB is assumed).

The HPMicro page lists ADC SMA input, motor-control/sensor interface, 2x20 IO header, onboard debugger and JTAG; the CAN transceiver is inferred from the RT-Thread CAN support (and a search summary also mentioned LIN/RS-485/RS-422, not included). USB-C PWR_DEBUG port with FT2232 is from the RT-Thread README. Board size and GPIO count are estimates.

boards.name: HPM6750EVKMINI
boards.description: Compact evaluation board for the dual-core 816 MHz RISC-V HPM6750 with on-board FT2232 debugger, Ethernet, USB, SDIO, QSPI flash and external RAM; about 298 RMB in China.
notes: Price is about 298 RMB converted (2022 listing); availability outside China is limited and orders go through HPMicro or Chinese distributors. HPM6750 has no internal flash: the board carries 8 MB QSPI flash and external DRAM (psramMB = 0 here because the DRAM size was not verified).

Not listed on HPMicro's current HPM6700 page (it shows the larger HPM6750EVK2, 146 x 102 mm), so the mini may be superseded; the EVKMINI is still in the RT-Thread BSP. Peripheral list (USB, Ethernet, QSPI, SDIO) is from the RT-Thread README. USB connector type, SD slot, size and GPIO count were not verified.

components.name: TPS54202
components.description: Cheap 28 V, 2 A synchronous buck in SOT-23-6: the default way to make 5 V or 3.3 V from a 12 V rail or a 3S/4S battery.
notes: Fixed 500 kHz with spread spectrum; FB reference 0.596 V.
28 V max: fine for 12 V and up to 5S Li-ion, too little margin for 24 V lead-acid systems.
Pin-compatible with TPS54302 (3 A) and LMR51430 (36 V).

en.note: Internal pull-up current (Ip 0.7 µA, +Ih 1.55 µA hysteresis); float EN to enable. Rising threshold 1.21 V typ, falling 1.19 V typ. Recommended operating max 5.5 V, so do not tie to VIN. Use open-drain logic to control. Optional UVLO divider R4 (VIN-EN) / R5 (EN-GND) per eq. 1-2; typical app (Fig 7-1, 8-28 V in) µses R4 = 511k, R5 = 105k.

notes: Fixed 500 kHz (390-630 kHz), +/-6% spread spectrum; Eco-mode pulse skipping at light load (no FCCM option).
Internally compensated peak current mode. Keep crossover < 40 kHz; without Cff, fo ~= 3.95 / (VOUT x COUT) (eq. 14, COUT in F).
Cff (C6, across top resistor R2) = 1 / (2*pi*fo*R2) (eq. 16); 75 pF in the 5 V design. Not needed with high-ESR COUT; reduce it with medium-ESR COUT.
LMIN = VOUT*(VINmax-VOUT)/(VINmax*KIND*IOUT*fSW) (eq. 8); KIND up to 0.3 with ceramic COUT, 0.2 with higher-ESR caps. Table 7-2 L values are for VIN = 28 V.
Output cap: CO >= 2*dIOUT/(fSW*dVOUT) for load step (eq. 11); typical app 2 x 22 µF 25 V X7R.
Input: >10 µF ceramic decoupling (typical app 10 µF), optional 0.1 µF HF cap; add ~47 µF electrolytic bulk if the supply is more than a few inches away.
Datasheet suggests R2 (top) ~100k; 49.9 ohm R1 in series with the top resistor in Fig 7-1 is only a loop-injection point (optional).
Can run at 100% duty cycle while BOOT-SW > 2.1 V. Internal 5 ms soft start. Hiccup OCP (512-cycle wait, 16384-cycle restart). Low-side source current limit 3 A typ.
Datasheet gives no explicit VOUT range; catalog vout 0.6-26 V is not stated in the datasheet.
design.pages: SLVSD26C (Rev C, Feb 2026). Pin functions p3; abs max (EN 7 V, VIN 30 V, BOOT-SW 7 V) p4; recommended EN max 5.5 V p4; VFB 0.596 V, EN thresholds, Ip/Ih, I(LIM_HS) 3.2 A typ, fsw p5; tMIN_ON 110 ns p5 (timing table); EN/UVLO eq. 1-2 p9-10; R2 100k start p10 sec 6.3.8 and p14 sec 7.2.3.3; boot 0.1 µF + 100% duty p11 sec 6.3.10 and p14; typical app Fig 7-1 p13; Cin p14 sec 7.2.3.1; KIND, eq. 8 p15; Cout eq. 11-14 p15-16; Cff eq. 16 and Table 7-2 p16-17; bulk 47 µF p20.

components.name: TPS563201
components.description: Very cheap 17 V, 3 A synchronous buck in SOT-23-6 with D-CAP2 fast transient response, for 5 V/3.3 V rails from 12 V.
notes: 17 V max: not for 4S LiPo (16.8 V full) or anything above a 12 V rail.
Output limited to 7 V. D-CAP2 needs some output-capacitor ESR/ripple; follow the datasheet values.
TPS563208 is the forced-PWM (FCCM) twin.

en.note: Active high, must be pulled up to enable (internal ~1.5 MΩ pull-down, 1 µA). VENH 1.6 V, VENL 0.8 V. EN abs max 19 V = VIN abs max and EN rec. max 17 V = VIN rec. max, so EN may be tied to VIN. Typical app drives EN through a 10k series resistor (R3) from an external EN signal.

notes: D-CAP2 adaptive on-time control, internally compensated, no Cff needed (C4 position in Fig 7-1 is 'Not Installed'). Stable with ceramic / low-ESR output caps.

Use the L/COUT values in Table 7-2: LC double pole must sit below the internal high-frequency zero. Per-row L range (min/typ/max): 1.0-1.8 V: 1.5/2.2/4.7 µH; 2.5-3.3 V: 2.2/2.2/4.7 µH; 5-6.5 V: 3.3/3.3/4.7 µH. COUT (C8+C9) 20-68 µF for every row. lTable lUh is the TYP column.
Fixed RBOT = 10k (R2); VOUT = 0.768 x (1 + R1/R2) (eq. 2). Datasheet VOUT range 0.76-7 V (features).
Max recommended duty cycle 75%: minimum VIN = VOUT / 0.75 (sec 7.3). Minimum off time 220 ns typ (310 max). No minimum on-time is specified.
Current limit is valley-detect on the low-side FET; ilimA 4.2 A is the DC output current limit (3.3-5.1 A) measured at VOUT 1.05 V, L 1.5 µH, not a peak high-side limit.
Quasi-fixed 580 kHz in CCM; when VIN < 7 V and VFB is below reference, frequency may drop (min ~200 kHz) to extend on-time.
TPS563201 = Eco-mode pulse skipping at light load; TPS563208 is the FCCM variant (same pinout).
Input: ceramic >10 µF recommended (typical app 2 x 10 µF + optional 0.1 µF HF cap); voltage rating above max VIN.
Fig 7-1 labels the 1.05 V design with R1 = 3.09k, but Table 7-2 gives R1 = 3.74k for 1.05 V (3.09k gives 1.0 V). Internal 1 ms soft start; hiccup UVP at 65% (10 ms restart).
design.pages: SLVSD90B (Rev B, Sep 2024). VOUT range p1 features; pin functions p3; abs max (VIN/EN 19 V, VBST-SW 6 V) p4; rec. op. EN 17 V p4; VFB 0.768 V, EN thresholds/REN, Iocl 4.2 A, tOFF(MIN) 220 ns, fsw 580 kHz p6; frequency fold-back p12 sec 6.4.1; typical app Fig 7-1 p13; VOUT eq. 2 p14; Table 7-2 and COUT 20-68 µF p15; Cin >10 µF p15; boot 0.1 µF p16; 75% max duty p19 sec 7.3.

components.name: TPS54302
components.description: 28 V, 3 A synchronous buck in SOT-23-6 with internal compensation: a drop-in upgrade of the TPS54202 for heavier 5 V loads.
notes: Fixed 400 kHz with spread spectrum.
28 V max: fine for 12 V and up to 5S Li-ion, not for 24 V systems with charging spikes.
Pin-compatible with TPS54202.

en.note: Internal pull-up current (Ip 0.7 µA, +Ih 1.55 µA hysteresis); float EN to enable. Rising threshold 1.23 V typ, falling 1.16 V typ. Recommended operating max 5.5 V, so do not tie to VIN. Use open-drain logic to control. Optional UVLO divider R4 (VIN-EN) / R5 (EN-GND) per eq. 1-2; typical app (Fig 7-1, 8-28 V in) µses R4 = 511k, R5 = 105k.

notes: Fixed 400 kHz (290-510 kHz), +/-6% spread spectrum; Eco-mode pulse skipping below ~500 mA peak inductor current (no FCCM option).
Internally compensated peak current mode. Keep crossover < 40 kHz; without Cff, fo ~= 5.1 / (VOUT x CO) (eq. 14, CO in F).

Cff (C6, across top resistor R2) = 1 / (2*pi*fo*R2) (eq. 16); 75 pF in the 5 V design. Not needed with high-ESR COUT; reduce it with medium-ESR COUT. Table 7-2 labels this column C8 but it is the same feed-forward cap.
LMIN = VOUT*(VINmax-VOUT)/(VINmax*KIND*IOUT*fSW) (eq. 8); higher KIND allowed with ceramic COUT (design example µses 0.35), KIND = 0.2 with higher-ESR caps.
Output cap: CO >= 2*dIOUT/(fSW*dVOUT) for load step (eq. 11); typical app 2 x 22 µF 25 V X7R.
Input: >10 µF ceramic decoupling (typical app 10 µF), optional 0.1 µF HF cap; add ~47 µF electrolytic bulk if the supply is more than a few inches away.
Datasheet suggests R2 (top) ~100k; 49.9 ohm R1 in series with the top resistor in Fig 7-1 is only a loop-injection point (optional).
Can run at 100% duty cycle while BOOT-SW > 2.1 V. Internal 5 ms soft start. Hiccup OCP. High-side limit 4-6 A (5 A typ), low-side valley limit 4 A typ.
Datasheet gives no explicit VOUT range; catalog vout 0.6-26 V is not stated in the datasheet.
design.pages: SLVSDG6C (Rev C, Mar 2026). Pin functions p3; abs max (EN 7 V, VIN 30 V) and rec. EN max 5.5 V p4; VFB 0.596 V, EN thresholds, Ip/Ih, I(LIM_HS) 5 A typ, fsw 400 kHz p5; tMIN_ON 110 ns p5; EN/UVLO eq. 1-2 p10-11; R2 100k start p11 sec 6.3.8 and p15; boot 0.1 µF + 100% duty p12 sec 6.3.10; typical app Fig 7-1 p14; Cin p15; KIND and eq. 8 p16; Cout eq. 11-14 p17; Cff eq. 16 p18; Table 7-2 p18; 47 µF bulk p21.

components.name: TPS62933
components.description: 30 V, 3 A synchronous buck in a tiny SOT-583 with 12 µA quiescent current and adjustable 200 kHz–2.2 MHz switching: good for battery robots.
notes: RT pin: float = 500 kHz, GND = 1.2 MHz, or a resistor for 200 kHz–2.2 MHz.
Pin 7 is soft-start (SS) on TPS62933; the TPS62933P variant has a power-good pin there instead, TPS62933F is forced PWM.
0.5 mm pitch SOT-583: needs a fine-pitch stencil.

en.note: Internal pull-up current Ip = 0.7 µA (enabled when floating) plus Ih = 1.4 µA hysteresis current above threshold. Rising threshold 1.21 V typ, falling 1.17 V typ. EN abs max 6 V, recommended max 5.5 V, so EN must NOT be tied to VIN. The reference design µses a UVLO divider R1 = 511k (VIN-EN), R2 = 88.7k (EN-GND) for 8 V start / 7 V stop (the text says 80.7k; Eq. 4 gives about 86.6k, so the schematic's 88.7k looks right). Divider eqs: R1 = (VSTART*VEN_FALL/VEN_RISE - VSTOP) / (Ip*(1 - VEN_FALL/VEN_RISE) + Ih); R2 = R1*VEN_FALL / (VSTOP - VEN_FALL + R1*(Ip+Ih)). Check VEN = (R2*VIN + R1*R2*(Ip+Ih))/(R1+R2) < 5.5 V at max VIN. Datasheet recommends > 500 mV hysteresis when µsing external UVLO. For always-on, leave EN floating.

extras.note: Floating (> 280 kΩ) gives 500 kHz (450-550 kHz). RT = GND (< 1 kΩ) gives 1.2 MHz. With a resistor RT to GND (8.9k-111k) fSW(kHz) = 17293 x RT(kΩ)^-0.942 (Eq. 2), 200 kHz to 2.2 MHz; 500 kHz from the formula would be about 43 kΩ. RT is sampled only at power-up / EN toggle.

Required, do not float. tSS = CSS x VREF / ISS (Eq. 6), VREF = 0.8 V, ISS = 5.5 µA. The reference design µses 33 nF, about 5 ms (4.8 ms calc). Minimum 6.8 nF, which gives about 1 ms. There is no internal default soft-start on TPS62933 (only the PG variants TPS62933P/O have a fixed 2 ms).

notes: Peak-current-mode with internal compensation. No COMP pin.

Inductor: L >= (VIN - VOUT)/(fSW x K x IOUT_MAX) x VOUT/VIN (Eq. 16) at VIN_MAX. Use K = 0.2-0.6, best 0.4. The design example µses 6.8 µH for 5 V/3 A at 500 kHz (from 30 V). Keep ripple >= about 10% of 3 A to avoid subharmonic oscillation. Isat ideally >= IHS_LIMIT (5.8 A max).

Table 10-2 COUT values are EFFECTIVE (derated) capacitance. Minimum effective COUT at 500 kHz is 15 µF (3.3 V) and 10 µF (5 V, 12 V). The design example µses 2 x 22 µF 35 V X5R 1206 plus 100 nF on the output.
RFBT = (VOUT - VREF)/VREF x RFBB (Eq. 1). Recommended RFBB = 10k with RFBT in 10k-300k. Use 1% resistors.
CFF: optional across RFBT to improve transient/phase margin, especially when RFBT > 100k. The design example says a 10 pF can be mounted (shown DNP on the schematic).
Input: 10 µF typical decoupling plus 0.1 µF VIN-GND directly at the pins. The design example µses 2 x 10 µF 50 V X7R 1206 plus 100 nF. Cap voltage rating must exceed VIN max.
BST: 0.1 µF X5R or better, >= 16 V. An optional series resistor < 10 Ω between BST and the cap reduces SW spikes (the reference design places R4 = 0 Ω).
Frequency foldback at minimum on-time. Approximate VIN max before foldback = VOUT/(tON_MIN x fSW) (Eq. 13).
PFM at light load (TPS62933). The TPS62933F variant is FCCM.
IHS_LIMIT 4.2/5/5.8 A min/typ/max. Low-side (valley) limit 3.8 A typ.
VFB 0.8 V +/-1% at 25 C (784-816 mV over -40 to 150 C). 98% max duty cycle is from the Features list.
SS must never be left floating (What to Do list p38).
design.pages: SLUSEA4D (Aug 2022). Pin functions Table 7-1 p3-4 (RT float=500k, SS min 6.8 nF, BST 100 nF); abs max p5 (EN 6 V, VIN 32 V); EC p6-7 (VFB 0.8 V, IHS_LIMIT 5 A typ, tON_MIN 70 ns, tOFF_MIN 140 ns, fSW 500 kHz RT float, ISS 5.5 µA, Ip 0.7 µA/Ih 1.4 µA, VEN 1.21/1.17 V); Features p1 (98% duty); FB Eq.1 + RFBB 10k p19; RT Eq.2 + Table 9-1 p20; UVLO Eq.3-5 p21; SS Eq.6 p22; Fig 10-1 reference design p28; BST/SS selection p29; UVLO setpoint, K 20-60% (best 40%), Eq.16 p30; L example + 10% ripple rule p31; COUT, Table 10-2, CIN 10 µF + 0.1 µF p32; CFF 10 pF p33.

components.name: TPS62160
components.description: 17 V, 1 A synchronous buck in a 2×2 mm WSON with power-good and 17 µA quiescent current, for small 3.3 V logic rails from 5–12 V.
notes: DCS-Control at ~2.25 MHz: 2.2 µH inductor, small ceramics.
17 V max: 12 V rails and up to 3S LiPo only.
Fixed-output versions exist (TPS62162 = 3.3 V, TPS62163 = 5 V).

en.note: Abs max is VIN + 0.3 V (VIN abs max 20 V), so EN can tie straight to VIN. The typical app (Fig. 7) does this. Logic input: high >= 0.9 V (0.6 V typ), low <= 0.3 V. Internal ~400 kΩ pull-down is connected while EN is low. Leakage 0.01 µA typ. No internal pull-up, so do not float.

pg.note: Open drain. Pull up to any voltage < 7 V (typical app: 100k R3 to VOUT). Sinks 2 mA at spec low level, 10 mA abs max sink. High-Z when off (EN low, UVLO, thermal shutdown). Rising threshold 95% VOUT, falling 90%. If unused, connect to GND or leave floating.

notes: DCS-Control, internally compensated. Nominal 2.25 MHz in PWM; the frequency varies with VIN/VOUT/L. PSM at light load (enters when IOUT < dIL/2).

R1 (top) = R2 x (VOUT/0.8 V - 1) (Eq. 6). Divider current must be >= 2 µA, so R2 <= 400 kΩ. Lower values give the best accuracy/robustness. TI's adjustable examples µse R2 = 150-200k (Figs 38-40) and 180k (Fig 36). If FB opens, VOS is clamped near 7.4 V.
Internal 25 pF feed-forward cap VOS-FB: fzero = 1/(2 pi R1 25 pF), fpole = 1/(2 pi 25 pF) x (1/R1 + 1/R2). External CFF is optional (not in the typical app).

Proven LC combos (Table 2, nominal values): 2.2 µH with 10/22/47/100/200 µF; 3.3 µH with 10/22/47/100 µF. Standard: 2.2 µH + 22 µF. Min inductor 2.2 µH; µse 3.3 µH at low VIN to get full output current. Output cap X5R/X7R ceramic.

Inductor peak: IL(max) = IOUT(max) + dIL/2, where dIL = VOUT x (1 - VOUT/VIN(max)) / (L(min) x fSW) (Eq. 7-8). Add ~20% margin to the saturation rating. Dynamic HS peak = ILIMF + (VIN - VOUT) x 30 ns / L.
ILIMF (HS static current limit) is 1.45/1.95/2.45 A min/typ/max. Low-side limit ~1.2 A typ.
Fixed on-time in PSM ~ VOUT/VIN x 420 ns, with an absolute minimum ~80 ns (approximate, not in the EC table). 100% duty mode: VIN(min) = VOUT + IOUT x (RDS(on) + RL).
Input 10 µF ceramic (typical app: 10 µF 25 V 0805), placed between VIN and PGND. Output 22 µF 6.3 V 0805.
Internal soft start: ~50 µs delay, then VOUT rises at ~25 mV/us. No SS pin.
Fixed-voltage siblings TPS62161/2/3 (1.8/3.3/5 V) share the pinout; on those, FB goes to AGND.
Layout: single-point ground at the thermal pad. FB/VOS traces short and away from SW.

components.name: TPS62130
components.description: 17 V, 3 A synchronous buck in a 3×3 mm QFN with power-good, soft-start/tracking and pin-selectable 2.5/1.25 MHz, for compact 3.3 V/5 V rails.
notes: FSW pin: low = 2.5 MHz, high = 1.25 MHz (better efficiency).
17 V max: 12 V rails and up to 3S LiPo only.
Output limited to 6 V.

en.note: Abs max is VIN + 0.3 V (AVIN/PVIN abs max 20 V), so EN can tie straight to VIN. The typical app (Fig. 9-1) ties EN to AVIN/PVIN. Logic: high >= 0.9 V (0.65 typ), low <= 0.3 V. EN must be driven high or low; the internal ~400k pull-down only holds a pin that was low and then floats (it disconnects when EN is high). Do not rely on floating.

pg.note: Open drain. Pull up to any voltage < 7 V (typical app: 100k R3 to VOUT). Sinks 2 mA at spec low level, 10 mA abs max. TPS62130: high-Z when off. TPS62130A: PG low when off. Thresholds 95% rising / 90% falling. If unused, connect to GND or leave floating.

extras.note: Low = 2.5 MHz typ (default for this design). High = 1.25 MHz for efficiency: tie to VOUT or PG, NOT VIN (7 V abs max). It must start Low to limit inrush, which a VOUT/PG connection gives. Use L >= 2.2 µH at 1.25 MHz. Internal ~400k pull-down only holds a pin that was set low and then floats.
Low = nominal VOUT. High = VOUT + 5% (margining): tie to VOUT or PG, not VIN (7 V abs max). Internal ~400k pull-down when floating after being set low.

Soft-start: CSS = tSS x 2.5 µA / 1.25 V (Eq. 10), ISS/TR = 2.5 µA typ. The typical app µses 3.3 nF, about 1.65 ms. Leaving SS/TR open gives the fastest start-up (allowed). It can also take a tracking voltage (VFB ~ 0.64 x VSS/TR, 50 mV-1.2 V). Abs max VIN + 0.3 V.
Output sense and control-loop input. Connect at the output capacitor by the shortest path, away from the inductor. An internal 25 pF feed-forward cap sits between VOS and FB.

Control supply. Must be fed from the same source as PVIN (pins 11, 12). The 0.1 µF (cinHf) must sit at AVIN to AGND to avoid noise coupling. An optional RC low-pass PVIN to AVIN is allowed but not required.

notes: DCS-Control, internally compensated. 2.5 MHz (FSW Low) or 1.25 MHz (FSW High) nominal in PWM. PSM at light load.

R1 (top) = R2 x (VOUT/0.8 V - 1) (Eq. 6). Divider current must be >= 2 µA, so R2 <= 400 kΩ. Lower values are recommended for accuracy. The only adjustable example in the datasheet (2.5 V, Fig. 9-45) µses R1 = 390k, R2 = 180k.
Internal 25 pF feed-forward cap VOS-FB: fzero = 1/(2 pi R1 25 pF), fpole = 1/(2 pi 25 pF) x (1/R1 + 1/R2). External CFF is optional, not in the typical app.

Proven LC combos (Table 9-2, nominal): 1 µH with 22/47/100/200 µF; 2.2 µH with 10/22/47/100/200 µF; 3.3 µH with 10/22/47/100 µF. Standard: 2.2 µH + 22 µF. 1 µH only with FSW Low. Use 2.2 µH for FSW High or low VIN. The typical app labels L as '1 / 2.2 µH'; its component list µses 2.2 µH XFL4020-222.
Inductor peak: IL(max) = IOUT(max) + dIL/2, where dIL = VOUT x (1 - VOUT/VIN(max)) / (L(min) x fSW) (Eq. 7-8). Add ~20% margin. Dynamic HS peak = ILIMF + (VIN - VOUT) x 30 ns / L.
ILIMF (HS static) is 3.6/4.2/4.9 A min/typ/max. Low-side limit 3.5 A typ. Below 0.5 V output, the limit drops to 1.6 A.
On-time ~ VOUT/VIN x 400 ns (FSW Low), with an absolute minimum ~80 ns (approximate, text only). 100% duty mode supported.
Input 10 µF ceramic (1210, 25 V in typical app) at PVIN-PGND plus 0.1 µF at AVIN-AGND (required). Output 22 µF 6.3 V 0805 X5R/X7R.
Pin list: AVIN (10) and PVIN (11, 12) are separate pins that are both 'VIN'. Thermal pad must be soldered.

components.name: TPS54360
components.description: 60 V, 3.5 A non-synchronous buck with Eco-mode, for robots running on 24 V, 36 V or 48 V packs that need a few amps of 5 V or 12 V.
notes: Non-synchronous: needs an external 60 V Schottky diode (e.g. B560C).
RT resistor sets 100 kHz–2.5 MHz (500 kHz with 200 kΩ); external compensation on COMP.
Solder the PowerPAD to GND with thermal vias.

en.note: Internal pull-up I1 = 1.2 µA (float = enabled) plus Ihys = 3.4 µA sourced once EN > 1.2 V. Threshold 1.2 V (1.1-1.3). Abs max 8.4 V, so never tie EN to VIN. The typical app µses a UVLO divider: RUVLO1 = 523k (VIN-EN), RUVLO2 = 84.5k (EN-GND) for 8 V start / 6.25 V stop. Eq.4 RUVLO1 = (VSTART - VSTOP)/Ihys; Eq.5 RUVLO2 = VENA / ((VSTART - VENA)/RUVLO1 + I1). If a low-start divider would push EN above 8.4 V at high VIN, add a zener clamp on EN. For always-on, leave EN floating.

comp.note: gmea = 350 µA/V (EA transconductance, normal operation; 77 µA/V in EC / 78 µA/V in text during soft-start). gmps = 12 A/V (COMP-to-SW current). EA dc gain 10,000 V/V, min unity-gain BW 2500 kHz, source/sink +/-30 µA. Datasheet method (Sec 8.2.2.11, Type 2A network: R4 in series with C5 from COMP to GND, optional C8 COMP to GND): Eq.44 fp(mod) = IOUT(max) / (2 pi x VOUT x COUT); Eq.45 fz(mod) = 1 / (2 pi x RESR x COUT); Eq.46 fco = sqrt(fp(mod) x fz(mod)); Eq.47 fco = sqrt(fp(mod) x fSW/2); µse the lower of Eq.46/Eq.47 as the initial crossover; Eq.48 R4 = (2 pi x fco x COUT / gmps) x (VOUT / (VREF x gmea)); Eq.49 C5 = 1 / (2 pi x R4 x fp(mod)); Eq.50 C8 = COUT x RESR / R4; Eq.51 C8 = 1 / (R4 x fSW x pi); µse the larger of Eq.50/51 for C8 (optional compensation pole). Use derated COUT. The method ignores slope compensation (actual fco ends up lower) and assumes fco lies between fp(mod) and fz(mod), with fz >= 10 x fp. Example (5 V, 3.5 A, 600 kHz, COUT 2x47 µF derated to 58.3 µF, RESR 2.5 mOhm): fp 1912 Hz, fz 1092 kHz, fco 23.9 kHz, R4 = 13.0k, C5 = 6800 pF (6404 calc), C8 = 39 pF. Type 1 (C2 only) or Type 2B are alternatives (Fig 30). Type 1 suits high-ESR electrolytic/tantalum output caps.

extras.note: A resistor is required (no default/float frequency). Eq.7: RT(kΩ) = 101756 / fSW(kHz)^1.008 gives 193.6k for 500 kHz, so µse E96 196k (Eq.8 fSW = 92417 / RT^0.991 gives about 494 kHz). The EC table specifies RT = 200k as 500 kHz typ (450-550). Range 100-2500 kHz. Check fSW against Eq.9 (min on-time pulse skip) and Eq.10 (foldback, divide by 8). Can sync to an external clock (160-2300 kHz).

notes: Asynchronous: needs an external Schottky catch diode SW to GND. Peak-current-mode, external compensation on COMP.
Internal soft-start: 1024 switching cycles, tSS(ms) = 1024 / fSW(kHz) (Eq.6), 2.1 ms at 500 kHz (10-90%). No SS pin.
RHS = RLS x (VOUT - 0.8 V)/0.8 V (Eq.3). The example µses RLS = 10.2k, RHS = 53.6k for 5 V. Divider current must be > 1 µA, so RLS < 800 kΩ.

Inductor: LO(min) = (VIN(max) - VOUT)/(IOUT x KIND) x VOUT/(VIN(max) x fSW) (Eq.28). KIND up to 0.3 for ceramic COUT, 0.2 for higher-ESR caps. Ripple must stay > 150 mA for stable PWM. Conservative choice: Isat >= switch current limit (5.5 A nominal).

COUT from three criteria: Eq.32 COUT > 2 x dIOUT / (fSW x dVOUT); Eq.33 overshoot COUT > LO x (IOH^2 - IOL^2)/(Vf^2 - Vi^2); Eq.34 ripple COUT > 1/(8 fSW) x 1/(VORIPPLE/IRIPPLE); Eq.35 RESR < VORIPPLE/IRIPPLE. Use derated values.

Design example (Fig. 34) is at 600 kHz, not 500 kHz: 5 V/3.5 A, VIN 8.5-60 V, RT 162k, L 8.2 µH (WE 7447797820), COUT 2 x 47 µF 10 V ceramic, CIN 2 x 2.2 µF 100 V, D1 B560C, Cboot 0.1 µF, UVLO 523k/84.5k, FB 53.6k/10.2k, COMP 13.0k + 6800 pF // 39 pF.
Input: X5R/X7R ceramic with at least 3 µF EFFECTIVE (after DC bias), rated above VIN max. The example µses 2 x 2.2 µF 100 V. Bulk is optional.

BOOT: 0.1 µF X5R/X7R, >= 10 V. 100% duty capable while BOOT-SW > 2.1 V; an integrated LS FET recharges BOOT (disabled above 24 V output). Min VIN (Eq.1): VIN(min) = (VOUT + VF + Rdc x IOUT)/0.99 - VF + RDS(on) x IOUT.
Current limit 5.5 A typ (4.5 min, 6.8 max, open loop). Min controllable on-time 135 ns typ. fSW(max skip) = 1/tON x (IO x Rdc + VOUT + Vd)/(VIN - IO x RDS(on) + Vd) (Eq.9).
Pulse-skip Eco-mode at light load. Catalog '500 kHz' is not an internal default: RT must be fitted.

components.name: LMR33630
components.description: 36 V, 3 A synchronous buck with power-good, 25 µA quiescent current and internal compensation, for 24 V robots and 6S–8S LiPo packs.
notes: Frequency is fixed by the part number: A = 400 kHz, B = 1.4 MHz, C = 2.1 MHz.
1 V reference, so the output can't go below 1 V.
Two VIN and two PGND pins: place input caps on both sides.

en.note: Pin table: 'Can be connected directly to VIN; do not float.' EN abs max is VIN + 0.3 V (VIN abs max 38 V). Precision enable: VEN-H 1.231 V typ rising (1.2-1.26), 100 mV hysteresis; above VEN-VCC-H (1 V) the VCC LDO turns on (standby), below VEN-VCC-L (0.3 V) full shutdown. Optional UVLO divider (Eq. 10): pick RENB 10-100 kΩ, RENT = (VON/VEN-H - 1)*RENB, VOFF = VON*(1 - VEN-HYS/VEN-H).

pg.note: Open-drain NMOS. Pull up to a logic rail, or to VCC or VOUT through 100 kΩ (sec. 8.3.1 / 9.2.2.8). Recommended max 18 V and never more than VIN + 0.3 V. Leave floating if unused. Low below 92 % (falling) / high above 94 % (rising) of VFB; over-voltage trip 107 %/105 %. ~4 ms PG delay at start-up, 60-170 µs glitch filter. Keep DC sink current < 5 mA. Forced low when EN is low (valid down to VIN = 2 V).

extras.note: Internal 5 V LDO output; requires a high-quality 1 µF, 16 V ceramic to GND. Do not load (a PG pull-up is OK) and never short it.

notes: Peak-current-mode, internally compensated. Frequency is fixed by the variant: A = 400 kHz (340-460), B = 1.4 MHz, C = 2.1 MHz. Auto PFM/PWM (diode emulation at light load), 4 ms internal soft start (2.9-6 ms), hiccup if FB < 0.4 V in current limit (94 ms off).

Timing (DDA/HSOIC): tON-MIN 75 ns typ (108 max), tOFF-MIN 50 ns typ (85 max); RNX/VQFN 68 / 52 ns. Frequency folds back when tON-MIN is reached (onset VIN ~ VOUT/(tON*fSW)) and in dropout, down to ~140 kHz. DMAX 98 % (system spec, in dropout).
Current limits: high-side ISC 4.5 A typ (3.85-5.05), low-side valley ILIMIT 3.5 A typ (2.9-4.1); IOUT(max) ~ (ILIMIT + ISC)/2 (Eq. 1).

Inductor (Eq. 4): L = (VIN - VOUT)/(fSW*K*IOUTmax) * VOUT/VIN with K = 0.2-0.4 (0.3 best). Use the device max current (3 A) for IOUTmax even if the load is smaller. Minimum L (Eq. 5): LMIN >= 0.28*VOUT/fSW (H, Hz), i.e. ripple >= ~10 % of rated current. Isat should be >= ISC; never below ILIMIT.

Output caps: ceramic X5R or better, effective values. COUT >= dIOUT/(fSW*dVOUT*K) * [(1-D)*(1+K) + K^2/12*(2-D)]; ESR <= (2+K)*dVOUT / (2*dIOUT*[1 + K + K^2/12*(1 + 1/(1-D))]); D = VOUT/VIN (Eq. 6). Ripple Vr ~ dIL*sqrt(ESR^2 + 1/(8*fSW*COUT)^2) (Eq. 7). Total COUT max ~10x the design value or 1000 µF, whichever is smaller. Use >= 10 V caps for VOUT <= 3.3 V, >= 16 V for VOUT >= 5 V. A 1-100 nF small ceramic on VOUT helps HF spikes.

Feedback: RFBT 100 kΩ recommended (max 1 MΩ), RFBB = RFBT/(VOUT/VREF - 1) (Eq. 3). If RFBT = 1 MΩ a CFF is mandatory. CFF is 'open' in all of Table 9-2, so it is optional; starting value from Eq. 9: CFF < VOUT*COUT / (120*RFBT*sqrt(VREF/VOUT)), then try smaller values.

Input: >= 10 µF ceramic required, rated >= max VIN (preferably 2x), plus a small-case 220 nF X7R as close as possible to VIN/PGND (mandatory HF bypass). IRMS ~ IOUT/2. Add a 20-100 µF electrolytic if supply leads are long.
Table 9-2 (1.4 MHz B version): 3.3 V -> 2.2 µH, 2x22 µF; 5 V -> 2.2 µH, 2x22 µF; 12 V -> 4.7 µH, 4x10 µF (same RFBT/RFBB, 10 µF + 220 nF in, 100 nF boot, 1 µF VCC, CFF open).
Do not let VOUT exceed VIN or go below ground. Layout: input cap loop as small as possible; CBOOT and CVCC close; FB divider close to FB pin.
Catalog check: VIN 3.8-36 V, VOUT 1-24 V (rec. op.; footnote says up to 95 % of VIN on request, TI product page lists 34 V max), 3 A, 400 kHz for the A version all agree with the datasheet.

components.name: LMR36510

extras.note: Internal 5 V LDO output; requires a high-quality 1 µF, 16 V ceramic to PGND. Do not load (a PG pull-up is OK).

notes: Peak-current-mode, internally compensated, fixed 400 kHz (340-460). LMR36510ADDAR = auto PFM/PWM (diode emulation at light load); LMR36510FADDAR = FPWM. 4.5 ms internal soft start; hiccup if FB < 0.4 V in current limit.

tON-MIN 92 ns typ, tOFF-MIN 80 ns typ (102 max), tON-MAX 7 µs; DMAX 98 % (system spec, frequency folds back to ~140 kHz in dropout). Frequency also folds back once tON-MIN is reached: VIN <= VOUT/(tON*fSW) (Eq. 2).

Current limits: high-side ISC 2.0 A typ (1.6-2.4), low-side valley ILS-LIMIT 1.3 A typ (1.0-1.6). Max load (Eq. 1): IOUT(max) = ILIMIT + (VIN - VOUT)/(2*fSW*L) * VOUT/VIN. Inductor Isat ideally >= ISC, never below ILIMIT.

Inductor (Eq. 4): L = (VIN - VOUT)/(fSW*K*IOUTmax) * VOUT/VIN, K = 0.2-0.4 (0.3 best; design example µses K = 0.4 at 24 V in -> 24.7 µH -> 22 µH). Use the device max current (1 A). Subharmonic limit (Eq. 5): LMIN >= 0.625*VOUT/fSW (H, Hz).

Output caps: ceramic X7R or better, effective values. Same COUT / ESR equations as LMR33630 (Eq. 6): COUT >= dIOUT/(fSW*dVOUT*K) * [(1-D)*(1+K) + K^2/12*(2-D)]. Max total COUT ~10x the design value or 1000 µF, whichever is smaller. Table 8-1 also lists minimum (size-optimised) COUT: 3.3 V 2x22 µF, 5 V 1x22 µF, 12 V 2x10 µF; the lTable µses the nominal (transient-optimised) values.

Feedback: RFBT 100 kΩ recommended (max 1 MΩ), RFBB = RFBT/(VOUT/VREF - 1). CFF 'None' in Table 8-1; mandatory if RFBT = 1 MΩ. Starting value (Eq. 9): CFF < VOUT*COUT / (120*RFBT*sqrt(VREF/VOUT)). Note: the application-curve BOM (Table 8-4) µses different dividers (3.3 V: 46.4k/20k; 5 V: 34k+46.4k/20k).

Input: >= 2.2 µF ceramic required (example 2.2 µF 100 V X7R), rated >= max VIN (preferably 2x), plus a small-case 220 nF 100 V X7R as close as possible to the IC. IRMS ~ IOUT/2. Optional 20-100 µF electrolytic for long input leads.
CBOOT: 100 nF, >= 16 V, BOOT to SW. Max die temperature 150 C. Do not let VOUT exceed VIN or go below ground.

Catalog check: datasheet rec. op. VOUT is 1-28 V (features list '1 V to 95 % of VIN'; TI product page says 62 V). Catalog voutMax 62 V matches the product page, not the rec. op. table. VIN 4.2-65 V, 1 A, 400 kHz agree.

components.name: LMR51430
components.description: 36 V, 3 A synchronous buck in SOT-23-6, pin-compatible with the TPS54202, for 24 V robots that want the cheap SOT-23 layout.
notes: X = 500 kHz, Y = 1.1 MHz; the XF/YF variants are forced PWM.
Pin-to-pin compatible with TPS54202/TPS54302, but with a 36 V rating.

Abs max is VIN + 0.3 V (38 V listed = VIN abs max); never drive EN with VIN at 0 V. Rising 1.227 V typ (1.36 V max), falling 1.08 V typ. Optional UVLO divider: VIN_RISING = VENH x (RENT + RENB)/RENB; design example RENB = 200k, RENT = 768k gives 6.0 V rising / 5.3 V falling.

notes: Fixed-frequency peak current mode, internally compensated, no Cff in the typical app. X = 500 kHz (450-560 kHz), Y = 1.1 MHz; F suffix (XF/YF) = FPWM, no F = PFM at light load.
LMIN = (VINmax - VOUT)/(IOUT x KIND) x VOUT/(VINmax x fSW) (eq. 11); KIND 0.2-0.6, design example 0.3. Inductor saturation current must exceed the peak current limit.
Load-step sizing (eq. 14, eight clock cycles): COUT > (1/2) x 8 x (IOH - IOL)/(fSW x dVOUT_SHOOT) (gives 48 µF for 1.5 A step, 250 mV, 500 kHz); ripple eq. 12-13. Design example: 2 x 22 µF 25 V X7R.
lTable is Table 9-1 (500 kHz, ceramic). Table 9-2 for 1.1 MHz (Y): 3.3 V 2.2 µH 2x10 µF; 5 V 3.3 µH 2x10 µF; 12 V 6.8 µH 3x10 µF; same 100k top / 22.1k, 13.7k, 5.23k bottom.
Feedback: VOUT = 0.6 x (1 + RFBT/RFBB); recommended RFBT range 10k-100k, do not exceed 1 MΩ. Tables µse RFBT = 100k.

Input: >= 4.7 µF X5R/X7R ceramic, voltage rating ~2x VINmax recommended; design µses 2 x 4.7 µF 50 V plus 0.1 µF HF cap close to pins (Fig 9-1 drawing shows 2.2 µF). Add 10-22 µF electrolytic bulk if the supply is more than a few inches away.
VOUT range 0.6 V to 95% of VIN (rec. op. conditions). tON_MIN 70 ns, tOFF_MIN 150 ns; frequency folds back (down to ~133 kHz) at min on/off time; DMAX 98%.
Current limits: high-side peak 4.76 A typ (3.67-6.68 A), low-side valley 3.5 A typ; IOUTmax ~= (ILS_LIMIT + ISC)/2. Hiccup after 256 cycles with FB < 40% VREF (135 ms off). Internal 4 ms soft start.
Boot cap 0.1 µF, 16 V or higher, X5R/X7R. Pin diagram calls the package DBV but orderables are SOT-23-THIN (DDC).

components.name: AP63203
components.description: Fixed 3.3 V, 2 A synchronous buck from up to 32 V in TSOT-23-6 with no feedback resistors and 22 µA quiescent current: the simplest MCU supply.
notes: Fixed 3.3 V: FB pin connects straight to the output.
1.1 MHz with spread spectrum; datasheet recommends 3.9 µH (2.2–10 µH allowed).
EN has a precise threshold, so a resistor divider sets an input UVLO.

en.note: Internal 1.5 µA pull-up from VCC: leave open or tie to VIN for automatic start-up (EN is a high-voltage pin, abs max 35 V = VIN abs max DC). Precision threshold 1.18 V rising / 1.10 V falling typ; an extra 4 µA hysteresis current flows above threshold. Optional VIN UVLO divider R5 (VIN-EN) / R6 (EN-GND): R5 = (0.932*VON - VOFF)/4.1 µA, R6 = 1.1*R5/(VOFF - 1.1 V + 5.5 µA*R5). Optional EN-GND delay cap: Cd[nF] = 1.27 * tdelay[ms].

notes: Peak-current-mode, internally compensated, fixed 1.1 MHz with +/-6 % frequency spread spectrum; PFM at light load (22 µA Iq); 4 ms internal soft-start.

Inductor: L = VOUT*(VIN-VOUT)/(VIN*dIL*fSW) with dIL = 30-50 % of the 2 A MAXIMUM load current (not the actual load); 2.2-10 µH for most applications; DC/saturation rating >= 35 % above max load; DCR < 100 mOhm. Datasheet table: 3.3 V -> 3.9 µH, C1 10 µF, C2 2x22 µF, C3 100 nF.
Output cap: 22-68 µF ceramic sufficient for most applications (typical 2x22 µF). Transient: COUT > L*(IOUT + dIL/2)^2 / ((dV + VOUT)^2 - VOUT^2) (Eq. 10).
Input cap: ceramic >= 10 µF sufficient for most applications; RMS rating > half the max load current; place close to VIN/GND.
Current limit: HS peak 2.8 A typ (2.5 min / 3.1 max); LS valley 3.2 A typ. Hiccup after 2 ms at current limit, restart after 16 ms.
Dropout: when VIN nears VOUT the HS switch is held on for multiple cycles (effective duty ~100 %, LDO-like) with forced BST refresh; no max-duty or min-off-time number is specified.
VIN 3.8-32 V (abs max 35 V DC, 40 V for 400 ms); UVLO rising 3.5 V typ, 440 mV hysteresis.
Layout: VIN cap as close as possible; 2 oz copper top/bottom and a GND plane under the device recommended for 2 A.

components.name: AP62300
components.description: Low-cost 18 V, 3 A synchronous COT buck in TSOT-23-6 or SOT-563 for 3.3 V/5 V rails from 5 V or 12 V inputs.
notes: 18 V max: fine for 12 V and 3S LiPo, marginal for 4S (16.8 V full).
The SOT-563 and TSOT-23-6 versions have different pinouts.
AP62301 is the PWM-only twin.

en.note: Internal 1.5 µA pull-up from VCC: leave floating for automatic start-up. Do NOT tie to VIN (EN abs max 8 V, VIN up to 18 V). Threshold 1.20 V rising (1.25 max) / 1.10 V falling; 5.5 µA hysteresis current above threshold. Optional UVLO divider R3 (VIN-EN) / R4 (EN-GND): R3 = (0.917*VON - VOFF)/5.625 µA, R4 = 1.1*R3/(VOFF - 1.1 V + 7 µA*R3), VON > 4.15 V, VOFF > 3.85 V. Optional EN-GND delay cap Cd[nF] ~ 0.278*td[ms].

notes: Constant-on-time (COT) control, internally compensated; tON = VOUT/(VIN*fSW); 750 kHz is the pseudo-fixed frequency at VIN 12 V, VOUT 5 V, CCM. AP62300 enters PFM at light load (AP62301 is the forced-PWM twin).

No peak/high-side current limit is specified: only a low-side VALLEY limit of 3.7 A typ (3.2 min / 4.2 max). Hiccup after 2.5 ms at the valley limit or FB < 495 mV; 20 ms off. ilimA left null for that reason.
Inductor: L = VOUT*(VIN-VOUT)/(VIN*dIL*fSW) with dIL = 30-50 % of the 3 A MAXIMUM load current; 1.2-4.7 µH for most applications; DC rating >= 35 % above max load; DCR < 30 mOhm.

Table 1 feed-forward cap C5 across R1 is optional: Open for 1.2/1.5 V, 10-100 pF for 1.8-5 V. Boot cap C6: 100 nF (<= 1.8 V), 100-220 nF (2.5 V), 100-330 nF (3.3/5 V); text: higher boot capacitance recommended when VOUT > 2.5 V.

Output cap: 22-68 µF ceramic sufficient for most applications (Table 1 µses 2x22 µF). Ripple dV = dIL*(ESR + 1/(8*fSW*COUT)); transient COUT > max(L*Itrans^2/(dVover*VOUT), L*Itrans^2/(dVunder*(VIN-VOUT))).
Input cap: ceramic >= 10 µF sufficient; RMS rating > half the max load current.
VOUT range 0.8-7 V (recommended operating). VIN 4.2-18 V, abs max 20 V DC / 22 V 400 ms; POR 3.9 V rising, UVLO 3.6 V falling.
Two packages with DIFFERENT pinouts: TSOT26 (AP62300WU-7) 1 GND, 2 SW, 3 VIN, 4 FB, 5 EN, 6 BST; SOT563 (AP62300Z6-7) 1 VIN, 2 SW, 3 GND, 4 BST, 5 EN, 6 FB. Same external circuit.
AP62300T (not this part) µses a 0.763 V reference with its own R1 column.
Layout: CIN tight across VIN/GND, inductor close to SW, feedback parts close to FB; many vias at GND and VIN pins; 2 oz copper recommended.
