components.name: MP1584EN
components.description: The 28 V, 3 A non-synchronous buck found on countless mini buck modules; adjustable 100 kHz–1.5 MHz, OK for repairs and clones of those boards.
notes: Not recommended for new designs: MPS points to the MP2338.
Non-synchronous: needs an external Schottky diode; FREQ resistor sets 100 kHz–1.5 MHz.
Rated -20 to +85 °C ambient.

en.note: Floating EN is pulled to ~3.0 V by an internal 1 µA source, so the chip also runs with EN open. Rising threshold 1.5 V typ (1.35-1.65), falling 1.2 V (300 mV hysteresis). The page-1 3.3 V app and Fig. 4 µse R5 100 k VIN->EN, R6 24.9 k EN->GND: VIN_on ~ 1.5 V*(1 + R5/R6) ~ 7.5 V. EN falls under 'All other pins -0.3 to +6 V', so size R6 so that EN stays <= 6 V at max VIN (100 k/24.9 k gives 5.6 V at 28 V). Datasheet advises programming the EN UVLO to >= VOUT + 3 V so BST stays charged at light load.

comp.note: GEA (error amp transconductance) 60 µA/V typ (40-80), GCS (COMP to current sense transconductance) 9 A/V, AVEA (EA voltage gain) 200 V/V. Datasheet: DC gain AVDC = RLOAD*GCS*AVEA*VFB/VOUT. Poles fP1 = GEA/(2*pi*C3*AVEA), fP2 = 1/(2*pi*C2*RLOAD); zero fZ1 = 1/(2*pi*C3*R3); ESR zero fESR = 1/(2*pi*C2*RESR); optional third pole fP3 = 1/(2*pi*C6*R3). Crossover fC ~ fS/10. Procedure: (1) R3 = (2*pi*C2*fC/(GEA*GCS)) * (VOUT/VFB); (2) C3 > 4/(2*pi*R3*fC) (fZ1 below fC/4); (3) C6 only if 1/(2*pi*C2*RESR) < fS/2, then C6 = C2*RESR/R3. Network: COMP -> R3 -> C3 -> GND (series), C6 COMP -> GND. Table 3 (VOUT / L / C2 / R3 / C3 / C6): 1.8 V / 4.7 µH / 47 µF / 105 k / 100 pF / none; 2.5 V / 4.7-6.8 µH / 22 µF / 54.9 k / 220 pF / none; 3.3 V / 6.8-10 µH / 22 µF / 68.1 k / 220 pF / none; 5 V / 15-22 µH / 22 µF / 100 k / 150 pF / none; 12 V / 22-33 µH / 22 µF / 147 k / 150 pF / none. COMP clamped 0.9-2.0 V; never pull COMP above 2.6 V.

extras.note: Rfreq(kΩ) = 180000 / [fs(kHz)]^1.1 -> 193 kΩ for 500 kHz (nearest E96 196 k). The datasheet's 500 kHz typical app (page 1) and the 1.8 V app µse 200 k (~485 kHz by the formula). EC table: 100 k -> 900 kHz. Range 100 kHz-1.5 MHz.

notes: NOT RECOMMENDED FOR NEW DESIGNS: the datasheet is watermarked 'Not recommended for new designs, refer to MP2338'.
Non-synchronous, peak-current-mode, external compensation on COMP; pulse-skipping at light load; fs set by FREQ resistor (100 kHz-1.5 MHz).
Current limit 4.7 A typ (4.0 min). Min on-time and min off-time both 100 ns (design-guaranteed).

Inductor: datasheet rule is ripple ~30 % of the MAXIMUM SWITCH CURRENT LIMIT (not of Iout; ~1.2-1.4 A), keep peak below the current limit. L = VOUT/(fS*dIL)*(1 - VOUT/VIN). Table 1 lists 3.3-22 µH parts. kInd left null because the rule is not Iout-based.

lTable lUh values are the UPPER end of the Table 3 inductor ranges (2.5 V 4.7-6.8, 3.3 V 6.8-10, 5 V 15-22, 12 V 22-33 µH); Table 3 does not state fs. The 3.3 V row matches the 500 kHz page-1 app (10 µH, 22 µF, 124 k/40.2 k). The 5 V Fig. 4 app µses 15 µH with Rfreq 100 k (~900 kHz). rTopK filled only where a datasheet schematic gives it.

Feedback: VOUT = VFB*(R1+R2)/R2. R2 typical 40.2 kΩ; with it R1 = 50.25*(VOUT - 0.8) kΩ (text: 127 k for 3.3 V; page-1 schematic µses 124 k). About 20 µA of BST-circuit current reaches the output at no load: keep R2 under ~40 k, i.e. IO + VO/(R1+R2) > 20 µA.
Input cap: ceramic preferred (typical 10 µF/50 V); RMS rating > half the load current. If electrolytic or tantalum is µsed, add a 0.1 µF ceramic close to the IC.
Output cap: ceramic, tantalum or low-ESR electrolytic allowed; datasheet circuits µse 22 µF (47 µF at 1.8 V) 6.3 V ceramic. With high-ESR caps add C6 per the comp procedure.

Bootstrap: 100 nF BST-SW. External bootstrap diode (1N4148 or BAT54) from a 5 V rail to BST recommended when VIN <= 5 V, VOUT/VIN > 65 %, or a 5 V rail exists. At light load keep VIN - VOUT > 3 V to refresh BST.
VIN 4.5-28 V (abs max 30 V), VOUT 0.8-25 V. Rated -20 to +85 C ambient.
Layout: minimise the CIN / high-side switch / Schottky loop; ceramic bypass at VIN; feedback and comp parts close to the IC and away from SW.

Datasheet inconsistency: Fig. 3 (1.8 V, VIN 4.5-28 V) µses R5 100 k / R6 59 k, which puts EN at ~10 V at 28 V VIN, above the 6 V 'all other pins' abs max (no EN clamp is documented). Prefer the 100 k / 24.9 k divider or leave EN floating.
design.pages: MP1584 Rev. 1.0 (8/8/2011); the MPS URL is behind a JS challenge, so the identical MPS PDF was read via the JLCPCB C15051 datasheet link. Page-1 typical app (3.3 V, 500 kHz: 10 µH, 22 µF, R1 124 k, R2 40.2 k, R3 68.1 k, C3 220 pF, R4 200 k, R5 100 k, R6 24.9 k, C4 100 nF, C1 10 µF/50 V) p1; abs max (VIN 30 V, BST-SW 6 V, all other pins 6 V) p2; EC table (VFB 0.8 V, ILIM 4.7 A, GCS 9 A/V, GEA 60 µA/V, AVEA 200, fosc 900 kHz @ 100 k, min on/off 100 ns, EN 1.5 V/300 mV) p3; pin functions p4; EN, COMP clamps, BST p8; Rfreq formula, 20 µA BST bleed p9; FB divider, inductor 30 % rule p10; Table 1 inductors, Table 2 diodes, Cin p11; Cout, compensation equations p12; Table 3 + R3/C3/C6 procedure p13; external BST diode, VIN-VOUT > 3 V p14; Fig. 3 (1.8 V) and Fig. 4 (5 V) apps p15; layout p16.

components.name: MP2315S
components.description: 24 V, 3 A synchronous buck in TSOT-23-8 with a selectable power-save (AAM) mode, the core of many 5 V mini modules and a good 12 V-to-5 V part.
notes: Next generation of the MP2315 (which is NRND); same TSOT-23-8 pinout.
AAM pin: resistor divider = power-save at light load, tie to VCC or float = forced CCM.
BST needs a capacitor plus a series resistor (10 Ω in every datasheet circuit).

en.note: Internal 1 MΩ EN-GND: a floating EN = OFF. EN has an internal 5.6 V series Zener clamp: pull up from VIN through a resistor that keeps EN current < 100 µA, RPULLUP >= (VIN - 5.6 V)/100 µA (e.g. 134 k at 19 V); all datasheet circuits µse 499 k VIN->EN. Driving EN directly (no resistor) requires the source to stay below 5.5 V. Rising threshold 1.4 V typ (1.26-1.54), 150 mV hysteresis.

extras.note: Internal 5.1 V LDO bypass: 0.1-0.22 µF, must be no more than 0.22 µF; place right at VCC/GND.
Tied to VCC: forced CCM, lowest ripple. For light-load power save µse the datasheet divider instead: 100 kΩ VCC→AAM, R5 AAM→GND (9.09 kΩ for 5 V, 7.5 kΩ for 3.3 V).

notes: Peak-current-mode, internally compensated, fixed 500 kHz (400-600). Current limit 5.5 A typ (4.5 min / 6.5 max, at 40 % duty); hiccup on UV (FB < 50 % of VREF). OVP at 120 % VREF.

Feedback (T-network): R1 = top (VOUT->tap), R2 = bottom, Rt = tap->FB. R2 = R1/(VOUT/0.791 V - 1). R1 fixed at 40.2 k for >= 1.8 V and 20.5 k for 1.2/1.05 V (Table 1). Table 1 values are based on a 44 µF output cap; other VIN, L or COUT may change R1/R2/Rt.
Feed-forward C5 across R1 in the typical circuits: 33 pF for 5 V and 3.3 V, 22 pF for 2.5/1.8/1.2/1.05 V.

Inductor: 1-10 µH with DC rating >= 25 % above max load; DCR < 20 mOhm for best efficiency; L = VOUT*(VIN-VOUT)/(VIN*dIL*fOSC) with dIL ~ 40 % of the MAXIMUM load current. Use larger L for loads below 100 mA.

BST: a capacitor AND a series resistor are required between BST and SW; all datasheet circuits µse 10 Ω + 0.1 µF (catalog note says ~20 Ω; the datasheet µses 10 Ω). Optional external 1N4148 from VCC to BST for VOUT 5 V/3.3 V or duty > 65 %; then BST cap 0.1-1 µF.
Input: 22 µF X5R/X7R ceramic sufficient for most applications, plus 0.1 µF (C1A) in the typical circuits; RMS rating > half the load current.
Output: ceramic, tantalum or low-ESR electrolytic allowed; typical circuits µse 2x22 µF ceramic.
VIN 4.5-24 V (abs max 26 V); VOUT 0.8 V to VIN*DMAX (DMAX 95 % typ, 90 % min). Fig. 9 (5 V out) is specified from VIN 6.5 V. UVLO 4.05 V rising, 750 mV hysteresis.
Abs max for VCC, AAM, FB, EN: 5.5 V ('all other pins'); EN is protected by its Zener + pull-up resistor.
Layout: CIN and its ground as short/wide as possible; VCC cap closest to VCC/GND; feedback/T-network close to the IC, SW away from FB.
design.pages: MP2315S Rev. 1.0 (12/21/2015); the MPS URL is behind a JS challenge, so the MPS PDF was read via the JLCPCB C3031493 datasheet link. components.name: SY8089A
components.description: Very cheap 5.5 V, 2 A synchronous 1 MHz buck in SOT-23-5 for making 3.3 V or 1.8 V from USB 5 V or a single Li-ion cell.
notes: 5.5 V max input (6 V abs max): only for 5 V or 1S Li-ion inputs.
EN must not float.
SY8089A (AAAC) has hiccup short-circuit protection; the SY8089 (AAC) latches off.

en.note: Do NOT float (no internal pull-up). Tie to IN for always-on: EN abs max is -0.3 V to VIN + 0.6 V (VIN abs max 6.0 V), so absMaxV 6.0 here means 'never above VIN + 0.6 V'. High > 1.5 V, low < 0.4 V. If driven by a source that goes hi-Z in shutdown while IN is on a battery, add 1 MΩ EN-GND pull-down.

notes: No BOOT pin: P-channel high-side switch (110 mOhm) + N-channel low side (80 mOhm). Internally compensated, 1 MHz fixed frequency, 100 % dropout operation.

Current limit: PFET current limit 3.5 A is a MINIMUM; the datasheet gives no typical value. SY8089A (AAAC): short circuit -> frequency folds back to ~30 % and current limit to 3.0 A (hiccup), OVP (>120 % for 20 µs) without latch-off. SY8089 (AAC) latches off instead.
Feedback: VOUT = 0.6*(1 + R1/R2), R1 = top; 10 k-1 M highly recommended for BOTH resistors. Typical app: R1 200 k / R2 100 k for 1.8 V with C1 22 pF across R1.
Feed-forward: 22 pF in parallel with R1 'may further speed up the load transient responses' and is recommended for large load steps (used in the typical app).

Inductor: L = VOUT*(1 - VOUT/VIN,MAX)/(FSW * IOUT,MAX * 40 %) (ripple ~40 % of max output current); Isat > IOUT,MAX + VOUT*(1-VOUT/VIN,MAX)/(2*FSW*L); DCR < 50 mOhm desirable. Typical app and EC conditions µse 2.2 µH. No allowed inductance range is stated.
Output cap: X5R or better, 6.3 V, greater than 22 µF (typical app 2x22 µF). No upper limit given.
Input cap: pin table says at least 10 µF ceramic; application text and typical app µse 22 µF X5R 6.3 V close to IN/GND.
VIN 2.7-5.5 V, abs max 6.0 V; UVLO max 2.5 V, 0.2 V hysteresis. Soft-start 1.2 ms. VOUT range not stated explicitly (catalog 0.6-5.5 V is consistent with VREF 0.6 V and 100 % duty).
Layout: CIN close to IN/GND, small LX copper, keep R1/R2 and FB trace away from LX; ground plane desirable.

components.name: LM2596
components.description: Classic 40 V, 3 A, 150 kHz non-synchronous buck in TO-263: robust and forgiving, but big and inefficient next to modern synchronous parts.
notes: Needs a 3 A Schottky diode and a large inductor (typ. 33 µH) plus bulk electrolytics.
ON/OFF pin is active-low: tie to GND for always-on.
5 mA quiescent current: poor for battery standby.

en.note: ~ON/OFF (pin 5) is active low: below ~1.3 V = regulator ON, above 1.3 V (up to 25 V max) = OFF (VIH/VIL 1.3 V typ at 25 C; ON guaranteed below 0.6 V, OFF above 2 V over temperature). Pin table: if shutdown is not needed, wire it to GND or leave it open; either way the regulator runs. Figures 9-10/9-13 tie it to GND, so tie to GND. The 25 V limit comes from the pin table and sec. 8.3.1/8.3.2 (the abs-max table has no ON/OFF row). Delayed start / UVLO circuits in sec. 8.3.1-8.3.2 (add 47 kΩ ON/OFF-GND if the Zener is > 25 V).

notes: Non-synchronous voltage-mode buck, internally compensated, fixed 150 kHz (127-173 kHz at 25 C, 110-173 over temp); frequency drops in second-stage current limit. VREF 1.23 V (1.193-1.267 at 25 C). Peak switch current limit 4.5 A typ (3.6-6.9 at 25 C). VSAT 1.16 V typ at 3 A. Max duty 100 %, no min on-time spec.

Inductor: µse the nomographs. Fixed versions: Fig 9-5/9-6/9-7 (max VIN vs load). ADJ: compute E*T [V*us] = (VIN - VOUT - VSAT)*(VOUT + VD)/(VIN - VSAT + VD)*1000/150 kHz with VSAT 1.16 V, VD 0.5 V (Eq. 8), then read Fig 9-8 at the max load. Fig 9-8 at 3 A (read off the graph): E*T ~13-20 -> 22 µH (L41), ~20-30 -> 33 µH (L40), ~30-44 -> 47 µH (L39), ~44-60 -> 68 µH (L44). Datasheet example: 28 V -> 20 V, 3 A, E*T 34.2 -> 47 µH (L39).

Common cases at 3 A: 12 V -> 5 V = 33 µH (L40), the datasheet's own example (Fig 9-6, Table 9-3 'VIN <= 15 V' row). 24 V -> 5 V = 47 µH (L39) from Table 9-3 ('VIN <= 40 V'). On Fig 9-6, 24 V sits just under the L39/L40 border at about 25 V (33 µH), and the ADJ E*T of 28 V*us also reads 33 µH, so 47 µH is the table's conservative pick. 12 V -> 3.3 V = 22 µH (L41): on Fig 9-5 the 33/22 µH border at 3 A is about 15 V, and the ADJ E*T of 16.8 V*us also gives 22 µH; Table 9-3 only has 10 V (22 µH) and 40 V (33 µH) rows. 24 V -> 3.3 V = 33 µH (L40). 24 V -> 12 V = 68 µH (L44) per Table 9-3 ('VIN <= 30 V'). At 2 A: 24 V -> 5 V = 68 µH (L38).

Ripple ratio implied by the nomograph (Fig 9-4): dIL is about 20-30 % of max load for 2-3 A designs, rising to 30-50 % at 0.5 A (kInd above = the 2-3 A band). Inductor current rating per Table 9-1 codes (L39-L41 = 3.5 A, L44 = 3.4 A, L38 = 3.1 A).

Output cap: low-ESR switching-grade aluminium electrolytic 82-820 µF (or solid tantalum 10-470 µF). Do not exceed 820 µF. Voltage rating >= 1.5x VOUT, often higher to get low ESR (a 16-25 V cap roughly halves the ripple of a 10 V one). ESR has both an upper limit (ripple) and a lower limit (too-low ESR, e.g. all-ceramic, can make the loop oscillate). Typical circuits: 220 µF 25 V (fixed) / 220 µF 35 V (ADJ) Nichicon PL; Table 9-3 gives 330 µF/35 V for 5 V at 3 A, VIN <= 15 V. Electrolytics are not recommended below -25 C (use tantalum). For ripple < ~15-20 mV add a post LC filter (1-5 µH + low-ESR cap).

Feed-forward cap (ADJ only): CFF across R2, required for VOUT > ~10 V and also µsed with very-low-ESR COUT (e.g. tantalum). Typically 100 pF to 33 nF; Eq. 10: CFF = 1/(31e3 * R2). Table 9-6 values by VOUT (through-hole electrolytic column): 2 V 33 nF, 4 V 10 nF, 6 V 3.3 nF, 9 V 1.5 nF, 12 V 1 nF, 15 V 680 pF, 24 V 560 pF, 28 V 390 pF (SMD tantalum column: 220 pF at 24-28 V). Use ceramic (not Z5U), film or silver mica. Eq. 10 and the table disagree: for the 20 V example (R2 15.4 k) the equation gives ~2.1 nF but the text picks 560 pF. Prefer Table 9-6.
R1 recommended 1 kΩ 1 % (range 240 Ω-1.5 kΩ) between FEEDBACK and GND; R2 = R1*(VOUT/VREF - 1). Example: 20 V -> R2 = 15.4 k.

Input cap: low-ESR aluminium electrolytic (or surge-tested tantalum) from VIN to GND, close to the IC. Size it by RMS ripple current >= 1/2 the DC load current (50 % at 40 C ambient, 75 % at 70 C), voltage >= 1.25x (sec. 9.1.1) to 1.5x max VIN for electrolytics, 2x for tantalum. Typical circuits µse 470 µF 50 V; the design examples pick 680 µF 35 V (12 V in) and 680 µF 50 V (28 V in). Be careful with high-K ceramic input caps: severe ringing at VIN. No separate small HF cap in the typical app.

Layout: heavy-line loops (CIN, diode, GND, COUT) short and wide, ground plane or single-point ground; keep the OUTPUT (switch) node copper small; FB divider near the IC; prefer closed-core (toroid/E-core) inductors, since open-core flux near FB/COUT causes ripple or instability.

Catalog check: VIN 4.5-40 V, ADJ VOUT 1.2-37 V, 3 A, 150 kHz, async all agree with the datasheet. The TI product page lists VOUT min 3.3 V (family-level), which does not apply to the ADJ part. The abs-max table oddly lists SD/SS, delay and flag pins (likely left over from a sister part); VIN abs max is 45 V.
The TO-263 tab is GND: solder it to at least 0.4 in² of copper (2 in² of 2 oz copper for full current).

components.name: XL4015
components.description: Cheap 36 V, 5 A, 180 kHz non-synchronous buck in TO-263-5, the chip on the popular 5 A adjustable buck/CC-CV modules.
notes: No enable or power-good pin.
The metal tab is SW, not GND: don't pour ground under it.
8 V minimum input; needs a Schottky diode (the datasheet uses a 10 A / 45 V MBRD1045G) and a 47 µH-class inductor.

extras.note: Internal regulator bypass: 1 µF ('105') from VC to VIN, NOT to GND (pin table: 'connect a 1uf capacitor to VIN'; CC in all app circuits).
TO263-5L metal tab is SW (pin 3), not GND: give it SW copper for heat, keep it out of the ground pour.

notes: Non-synchronous P-MOSFET (60 mOhm typ) buck, fixed 180 kHz (144-216 kHz), internally compensated; drops to 48 kHz under output short. Max duty 100 %, min dropout 0.3 V.
Switch current limit 7 A typ (VFB = 0 V); no min/max given.
Feedback: VOUT = 1.25*(1 + R2/R1), R2 = top, R1 = bottom. Datasheet circuits: 5 V 10 k/3.3 k, 12 V 13 k/1.5 k, 20 V 15 k/1 k, each with CFF 33 nF across R2. VFB 1.225-1.275 V.
Output: 330 µF/25 V electrolytic plus a 1 µF ('105') ceramic C2 in parallel in the 5 V and 12 V circuits; 470 µF/35 V + 1 µF in the 20 V/5 A circuit. No capacitance range is specified.
Input: 220 µF/50 V electrolytic CIN plus a 1 µF ('105') ceramic C1 VIN-GND (470 µF/50 V in the 20 V/5 A circuit). cinUf = the electrolytic bulk, cinHfNf = the 1 µF ceramic.
Inductor: 47 µH rated 5 A in all standard circuits; 47 µH rated 12 A in the 'high power' 20 V/5 A circuit. The datasheet gives no inductor equation or ripple target.
Schottky catch diode SW-GND is mandatory; GND pin should sit outside the diode-to-output-cap ground path to keep switching spikes out of the IC ground.
VIN 8-36 V operating, abs max 40 V; FB abs max 7 V. Iq 2.1 mA typ. Typical efficiency 87 % (12->5 V, 5 A), 93 % (24->12 V, 4 A).
No enable, power-good or soft-start pins.
The TO-263 tab is SW (pin 3), not GND: give it SW copper and keep it out of the ground pour.

components.name: TPS5430
components.description: Proven 36 V, 3 A non-synchronous 500 kHz buck with internal compensation in a PowerPAD SOIC-8, for 24 V robot rails.
notes: Needs an external Schottky diode (e.g. B340A).
Fixed 500 kHz voltage-mode PWM with no light-load mode: ~2 mA quiescent.
Pins 2 and 3 are NC; the PowerPAD must be soldered to GND.

en.note: ENA has an internal 1.5 MΩ pull-up; leave floating to run. Above 1.3 V (max) starts, below 0.5 V stops. Abs max 7 V, so never tie to VIN. Control only with open-drain/open-collector logic; do NOT connect a resistor from ENA to GND.

coutEq.note: Voltage mode, internal type III: keep crossover 3–30 kHz. COUT = 1 / (3357·L·fCO·VOUT) (eq. 8); ESRmax = 1 / (2π·COUT·fCO) (eq. 9).

notes: Voltage-mode control with input feed-forward (gain 25) and internal type III compensation (fp0 2165 Hz, fz1 2170 Hz, fz2 2590 Hz, fp1 24 kHz, fp2 54 kHz). Fixed 500 kHz (400-600 kHz), not adjustable. Non-synchronous: needs external Schottky catch diode PH-to-GND.

Default design µses an electrolytic / polymer output cap with defined ESR: Fig 7-1 µses one 220 µF Sanyo POSCAP 10TPB220M (10 V, 40 mOhm max ESR). Keep crossover 3-30 kHz: fCO = fLC^2 / (85 x VOUT) (eq. 7); COUT = 1 / (3357 x LOUT x fCO x VOUT) (eq. 8, 220 µF for 15 µH at 18 kHz, 5 V); ESRmax = 1 / (2*pi*COUT*fCO) (eq. 9); ESR zero must be above crossover but not far above the 24 kHz / 54 kHz internal poles at minimum ESR.
LMIN = VOUT*(VINmax - VOUT)/(VINmax*KIND*IOUT*fSW) (eq. 4); KIND 0.2-0.3; L typically 10-100 µH.

All-ceramic output is possible only with an extra external network (Fig 7-11, 3.3 V, 15 µH, 100 µF): LC resonance <= 7 kHz, CO(min) = 1/((2*pi*7000)^2 x LO) (eq. 16); FLC = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(LO*CO_eff)); Fp1 = 500000 x VO / FLC, Fz1 = 0.7 x FLC, Fz2 = 2.5 x FLC (2.3-2.7 ok); C7 = 1/(2*pi*Fp1*(R1||R2)) in series with R3 = 1/(2*pi*Fz1*C7) from VSENSE to GND; C6 = 1/(2*pi*Fz2*R1) across R1; C4 (< C6/10, 150 pF) VSENSE to GND. Example values: C7 0.1 µF, R3 549 ohm, C6 1500 pF, C4 150 pF, R1 10k, R2 5.9k.
Feedback: start with top R1 = 10k for any design; R2 = R1 x 1.221 / (VOUT - 1.221) (eq. 12). Minimum VOUT = 1.221 V.

VOUT limits: VOUTmax = 0.87 x ((VINmin - IOmax x 0.230) + VD) - IOmax x RL - VD (eq. 13, µses 87% min duty); VOUTmin = 0.12 x ((VINmax - IOmin x 0.110) + VD) - IOmin x RL - VD (eq. 14, tON(min) up to 200 ns). DMAX 87% min / 89% typ.
Boot cap must be 0.01 µF low-ESR X5R/X7R, rated >= 10 V (BOOT-PH can reach 6-10 V in operation).

Input: 10 µF X5R/X7R ceramic recommended (min 4.7 µF per layout section) placed within 1 mm of VIN and GND pins; add ~100 µF electrolytic bulk if the supply is more than a few inches away. Rec. VIN 5.5-36 V (UVLO 5.3 V typ).
Other datasheet examples: 10-35 V in, 5 V out: 22 µH, 220 µF POSCAP, Cin 2 x 4.7 µF, R1 10k / R2 3.24k (Fig 7-9). TPS5431 is the 23 V variant.
Catalog voutMax 31 V is not stated in the datasheet; it is roughly eq. 13 at 36 V in / 3 A (about 30.6 V with VD 0.5 V, RL 0).
Pins 2 and 3 are NC. Solder the exposed pad to GND.

components.name: LM5164
components.description: 100 V, 1 A synchronous COT buck with power-good and 10.5 µA quiescent current, for 48 V and 60 V+ robot or e-bike packs.
notes: RON resistor sets the switching frequency (up to 1 MHz; 300 kHz in the datasheet design).
Diode emulation at light load; the EP has no electrical connection, tie it to GND.
COT control needs some output ripple at FB; use the datasheet ripple-injection network with ceramic caps.

en.note: EN/UVLO abs max 100 V = VIN abs max; the typical application (Fig 7-1) ties EN/UVLO straight to VIN, and sec. 6.3.9 allows a logic drive or a direct VIN connection. Below 1.1 V: shutdown (3 µA); 1.1-1.5 V: standby (VCC on, no switching); above 1.5 V typ (1.45-1.55) rising / 1.4 V falling: run. Optional UVLO divider RUV1 (VIN-EN) / RUV2 (EN-GND): VIN(on) = 1.5 V*(1 + RUV1/RUV2), VIN(off) = 1.4 V*(1 + RUV1/RUV2); RUV1 ~1 MΩ recommended.

pg.note: PGOOD is open drain; pull up through 10-100 kΩ to a DC rail of no more than 14 V (use a divider from a higher rail). Releases when FB > 95 % of VREF (VPG-UTH 1.14 V), pulls low (25-30 Ω) when FB < 90 % (VPG-LTH 1.08 V); 5 µs rising-edge deglitch. The typical application leaves PGOOD unconnected.

extras.note: Sets the COT on-time / CCM frequency. Eq. 12/15: RRON[kΩ] = VOUT[V]*2500 / FSW[kHz]; equivalently FSW[kHz] = VOUT*2500/RRON (Eq. 1). On-time Eq. 11: tON[us] = RRON[kΩ] / (VIN[V]*2.5). Keep tON >= 50 ns at max VIN and FSW <= 1 MHz. Examples at 300 kHz: 3.3 V -> 27.5 k, 5 V -> 41.7 k, 12 V -> 100 k (typ. app). RON is noise sensitive: place RRON close, parasitic RON-GND capacitance <= 20 pF.

rippleInjection.note: Type 3 (datasheet sec. 7.2.2.6): RA from SW and CA to VOUT build a triangle; CB couples it into FB. CA ≥ 10 / (fsw·(RFB1‖RFB2)); RA·CA ≤ tON·(VIN − VOUT) / 20 mV; CB ≥ tsettle / (3·RFB1). C0G for CB.

notes: Constant on-time (COT), no loop compensation; nearly constant CCM frequency set by RRON (300 kHz in the typical app, up to 1 MHz). Diode emulation and pulse skipping at light load, ultra-low IQ sleep (10.5 µA) after 15 µs idle. Fixed 3 ms soft start. No VCC pin (internal bias, no external cap); internal boot diode.

Min controllable on-time 50 ns (rec. op. tON 50-10000 ns); min off-time 50 ns typ, forced to 250 ns when tON < 300 ns. Min duty DMIN = tON(min)*FSW (Eq. 16); VIN(max) before frequency foldback = VOUT/(tON(min)*FSW) (Eq. 17). Not in the EC table as a min/typ/max spec.

Current limit: high-side peak 1.5 A typ (1.25-1.75), low-side backup peak 1.5 A, foldback valley 1.2 A typ (0.95-1.4). Inductor saturation current must be well above the current limit. Rec. op. load 1 A nominal, 1.25 A max.
CBST must be 2.2 nF, 50 V X7R (abs max range 1.5-2.5 nF). A larger cap stresses and can damage the internal VCC regulator; a smaller one will not drive the HS FET.
Inductor (Eq. 20): LO = VOUT/(FSW*dIL) * (1 - VOUT/VIN(nom)) with dIL = 30-50 % of rated load at nominal VIN. Typical app: 68 µH (447 mA p-p at 48 V in, 45 %).
Output cap (Eq. 21): COUT = dIL / (8*FSW*VOUT(ripple)), with ripple <= 0.5 % of VOUT; ceramic X7R. Typical app 2x22 µF 25 V X7R (BOM Table 7-1; Fig 7-1 shows 47 µF).

Feedback: VREF 1.2 V (1.181-1.218). RFB2 = 1.2 V/(VOUT - 1.2 V) * RFB1 (Eq. 10); select RFB1 in 100 kΩ-1 MΩ (not above 1 MΩ). Typical app RFB1 453 k / RFB2 49.9 k for 12 V (BOM part number suggests 448 k, value column says 453 k).

Other ripple schemes (Table 6-1): Type 1 = resistor RESR in series with COUT, RESR >= VOUT*20 mV/(VFB*dIL(nom)) and RESR >= VOUT/(2*VIN*FSW*COUT) (Eq. 2-3). Type 2 = RESR plus CFF across RFB1: RESR >= 20 mV/dIL(nom), RESR >= VOUT/(2*VIN*FSW*COUT), CFF >= 1/(2*pi*FSW*(RFB1 || RFB2)) (Eq. 4-6). Type 3 (used) gives the lowest output ripple.

Input: high-frequency ceramic >= 2.2 µF X7R/X7S rated ~2x max VIN, close to VIN/GND (typical app BOM µses 2x 2.2 µF 100 V). IIN ripple / CIN Eq. 22-23. Add bulk if the source is more than ~5 cm away; a 10 µF electrolytic with ~0.5 Ω ESR damps most inputs.
Layout: minimise the CIN-VIN-GND loop; keep SW copper small; FB divider and ripple network close to FB; RRON close to RON.
Catalog check: VIN 6-100 V, 1 A, 300 kHz (typical app) and VOUT min 1.2 V (= VREF) agree. The datasheet does not state a maximum VOUT; the 90 V in the catalog comes from the TI product page.

components.name: Pololu D24V22F5 5 V step-down regulator
components.description: Tiny 5 V synchronous buck module (up to 36 V in, about 2.2–2.5 A) with enable and power-good, a solid drop-in 5 V supply for small robots.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Rated 2.2 A continuous at 24 V in (2.5 A typical max); less at higher input voltages.
Reverse-voltage protected; minimum input rises to about 5.8 V at 2.5 A.
Leave EN unconnected for always-on.

terminals.name: PG
terminals.note: Open-drain power-good output: pulled low when VOUT falls below ~85% of nominal, high-impedance once VOUT rises above ~90%. Needs an external pull-up resistor.

terminals.name: EN
terminals.note: Enabled by default: 270 kΩ on-board pull-up to reverse-protected VIN. Drive below 1 V to enter low-power state (~5-10 µA per volt on VIN). Leave unconnected if unused.

terminals.name: VIN
terminals.note: Silkscreen 'IN'. Up to 36 V; effective minimum is VOUT + dropout (5.3 V headline minimum for the 5 V version).

terminals.name: GND
terminals.note: Square pad in the main 5-pin row, between IN and OUT.

terminals.name: VOUT
terminals.note: Silkscreen 'OUT'. Fixed 5 V, ±4%.

notes: The five main pins are on one 0.1 in row in the order PG, EN, IN, GND, OUT, labeled on the top side. A 5x1 straight or right-angle header is included.
Dropout rises roughly linearly with load: about 0.25 V near 0 A to about 0.73 V at 2.5 A. These values are read from Pololu's dropout graph, not stated in text.
Has reverse-voltage protection (via a 40 V MOSFET, per the customization note), over-current/short-circuit protection, thermal shutdown and soft-start.
No-load quiescent current about 1 mA; with EN low, about 5-10 µA per volt on VIN.

Maximum continuous current depends on VIN and is thermally limited: about 2.5 A at 12 V in, falling to about 1.9 A at 36 V in (Pololu graph, still air, room temperature). The headline figure is 2.5 A.
Can get hot enough to burn you during normal operation.
Switching frequency about 400 kHz.
Two 2.18 mm mounting holes for #2 or M2 screws.

components.name: Pololu D36V28F5 5 V step-down regulator
components.description: 5 V, 3.2 A synchronous buck module for up to 50 V in, with enable, power-good and reverse protection: good for 24–36 V robots and 10S packs.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: 3.2 A typical max at 36 V in; 2.5–4 A depending on input voltage.
Reverse protection only to -40 V.
Power-save mode stays above 20 kHz (no audible whine).

terminals.name: EN
terminals.note: Enabled by default: 100 kΩ on-board pull-up to VIN. Below 1.2 V the regulator sleeps; above 1.35 V it turns back on. Sleep draws about 10-20 µA per volt on VIN. The tight threshold lets an external divider from VIN act as a precise low-battery cutoff.

terminals.name: VIN
terminals.note: Silkscreen 'IN'. Up to 50 V; effective minimum is VOUT + dropout (5.3 V headline minimum).

terminals.name: GND
terminals.note: Square pad.

terminals.name: VOUT
terminals.note: Silkscreen 'OUT'. Fixed 5 V, ±4%.

terminals.name: PG
terminals.note: Not on the edge row: second-row pad right next to EN, on the 0.1 in grid. Open-drain output that goes low when VOUT is more than 20% above or more than 10% below nominal (with hysteresis). Needs an external pull-up resistor.

notes: Edge row order is EN, IN, GND, GND, OUT. PG sits off the edge, beside EN. The labels are printed on the bottom side.
Includes a 6x1 straight header and a 5x1 right-angle header. One pin of the straight header can be broken off and soldered into PG.
Dropout for the 5 V version, read from Pololu's dropout graph (not stated in text): about 0.9 V at 0.5 A, 1.1 V at 2 A, 1.35 V at 3.2 A and 1.55 V at 4 A.
Reverse-voltage protection up to 40 V, which is below the 50 V input maximum.
Has output undervoltage and overvoltage protection, over-current and short-circuit protection, thermal shutdown and soft-start.
No-load quiescent current 2-3 mA typical. Light-load power-save mode keeps the switching frequency above 20 kHz (ultrasonic). Switching frequency is about 500 kHz under heavy load.
Maximum continuous current is about 4 A at about 7-12 V in, 3.2 A at 36 V in, and about 2.5 A at 48 V in (Pololu graph, still air, room temperature).
Can get hot enough to burn you during normal operation.
Two 2.18 mm mounting holes for M2 or #2 screws.

components.name: Pololu D24V50F5 5 V, 5 A step-down regulator

notes: No power-good output.

Switching frequency drops at light load, which can make filtering harder.

terminals.name: EN
terminals.note: Enabled by default: 100 kΩ on-board pull-up to reverse-protected VIN. Drive below 0.6 V to enter low-power state (~10-20 µA per volt on VIN). Leave unconnected if unused.

terminals.name: VIN
terminals.note: Up to 38 V; effective minimum is VOUT + dropout (6 V headline minimum).

terminals.name: GND
terminals.note: Square pad.

terminals.name: VOUT
terminals.note: Silkscreen 'OUT'. Fixed 5 V, ±4%.

notes: The five pins are on one 0.1 in row in the order EN, VIN, GND, GND, OUT, labeled on the top side. A 5x1 straight or right-angle header is included. This module has no power-good pin.
The text says dropout rises roughly linearly from about 0.7 V to about 1.5 V with load. Pololu's dropout graph shows about 1.15 V at 5 A.
Has reverse-voltage protection (no voltage limit stated), over-current and short-circuit protection, thermal shutdown, soft-start and under-voltage lockout.

The over-current limit depends on temperature. At low VIN with sustained loads well over 5 A (more than 5 s), the regulator might not shut off before it is damaged. Pololu suggests a fuse or circuit breaker in that case.
No-load quiescent current is 700 µA typical; with EN low it is 10-20 µA per volt on VIN.
Switches at about 600 kHz. Frequency drops at light load, which can make output noise harder to filter.
Can get hot enough to burn you during normal operation.
Two 2.18 mm mounting holes for #2 or M2 screws.

components.name: MP1584 mini adjustable buck module
components.description: Tiny (23×17 mm) adjustable buck board, 4.5–28 V in to 0.8–20 V out, for wiring a cheap 5 V or 3.3 V supply into a hobby robot.

variants.note: ProtoSupplies SKU; the same board is sold by many vendors

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Sold as 3 A, but plan for about 1.5 A continuous (2 A peak) without extra cooling.
Single-turn trimmer: set and check the output before connecting the load.
EN is not broken out on most versions.

terminals.name: IN+
terminals.note: Input voltage 4.5-28 V. Two holes per connection.

terminals.name: IN-
terminals.note: Input ground.

terminals.name: OUT+
terminals.note: Adjustable output, 0.8-20 V.

terminals.name: OUT-
terminals.note: Output ground, connected to IN- on the module (non-isolated).

adjust.direction: clockwise lowers Vout; counter-clockwise raises Vout

notes: Four solder connections, each with two holes or pads. Labels are on the back. Seen from the back: OUT- and IN- along one long edge, OUT+ and IN+ along the other, with an arrow pointing from IN to OUT.
Hole spacing is 0.1 in side-to-side but not end-to-end, so the module does not plug directly into a breadboard.

Typical dropout is 1.6 V, and the output can be set no higher than about VIN - 1.6 V (e.g. about 10.4 V from 12 V in). For best ripple, keep VIN at least 1.6-2 V above VOUT. The load condition for these figures is not stated.
The single-turn pot sets Vout to within a couple of percent (e.g. 4.95-5.05 V when aiming for 5 V).
Rated 1.5 A continuous and 2 A peak. The vendor does not recommend more than about 1.5 A long-term because of heat.
The IC has built-in over-current and thermal limiting. Reverse-polarity protection is not mentioned.
Uses ceramic capacitors, not electrolytics. Measured output ripple is 30-50 mV. Switching frequency is 1 MHz.
Wire the input and output before applying power, to avoid damaging the module. Components get hot under heavy load.

components.name: LM2596S adjustable buck module
components.description: Ubiquitous 43×21 mm LM2596S adjustable buck board, up to 40 V in and 1.25–35 V out, for quick bench and hobby supplies.

variants.note: ProtoSupplies SKU; the same board is sold by many vendors

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Advertised 3 A, but about 1.5 A continuous (2 A peak) without a heatsink.
Stores list 3.5 V minimum input; the LM2596 itself is rated from 4.5 V.
High output ripple (50–400 mV); add filtering for analog/sensor rails.

terminals.name: IN+
terminals.note: Input voltage, 3.5-40 V per the vendor page.

terminals.name: IN-
terminals.note: Input ground.

terminals.name: OUT+
terminals.note: Adjustable output, 1.25-35 V.

terminals.name: OUT-
terminals.note: Output ground, common with IN- (not isolated).

adjust.direction: clockwise raises Vout; counter-clockwise lowers Vout

notes: Set the output voltage before connecting a load. Modules µsually ship with the pot turned fully clockwise, so the output is close to VIN. It takes several counter-clockwise turns before the output starts to drop.
With the silkscreen upright, input is on the left end and output on the right end. The vendor text does not say which of IN+ and IN- (or OUT+ and OUT-) is on top.
Solder pads are not on a 0.1 in pitch, so the module does not plug into a breadboard. Two holes for M3 mounting screws.
The output can be set no higher than about VIN - 1.5 V (e.g. about 10.5 V from 12 V in). The load condition is not stated.
Rated 1.5 A continuous, 2 A short-term, 24 W maximum. The vendor does not recommend more than about 1.5 A long-term because the IC, capacitors and inductor get hot.
Output ripple averages about 300 mV (50-400 mV depending on load). The vendor suggests an extra output filter capacitor to reduce it and says the output is not ideal for driving logic directly.
The IC has built-in over-current and thermal limiting. Reverse-polarity protection is not mentioned.
Switching frequency is 150 kHz. Measured efficiency is 66-86%.
Wire the input and output before applying power. Components get hot under heavy load.

components.name: XL4015 adjustable 5 A buck module with voltmeter
components.description: XL4015 adjustable buck board with a built-in voltmeter and screw terminals, 1.25–32 V out at up to 4 A, for higher-current hobby rails.

variants.note: ProtoSupplies SKU; the same board is sold by many vendors

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Store rates it 4.5–38 V in / 1.25–35 V out; the XL4015 chip is rated 8–36 V in, 32 V out.
4 A continuous, 4.5 A max; fit the supplied heatsink above about 3 A.
Input has a reverse-polarity diode; the display draws extra current.

terminals.name: IN+
terminals.note: Screw terminal on the left end (display facing you), upper position. 4.5-38 V per the vendor page. Input has a reverse-polarity protection diode.

terminals.name: IN-
terminals.note: Screw terminal, left end, lower position. Ground.

terminals.name: OUT+
terminals.note: Screw terminal on the right end, upper position. Adjustable output, 1.25-35 V (derated to 35 V because of the 35 V output capacitor).

terminals.name: OUT-
terminals.note: Screw terminal, right end, lower position. Ground.

adjust.direction: clockwise raises Vout; counter-clockwise lowers Vout

notes: Screw terminals: input on the left, output on the right, when the LED display faces you.
The input has a reverse-polarity protection diode.
The output can be set no higher than about VIN - 1.5 V (e.g. about 10.5 V from 12 V in). The load condition is not stated.

Rated 4 A continuous and 4.5 A short-term, 75 W maximum. The vendor derates it from the 5 A sellers often claim. About 3 A is comfortable; above 4 A it runs hot. Keep the IC below about 80 °C for long-term µse.
A sudden excessive load can kill the XL4015 before thermal or current limiting reacts. Increase the load gradually.
Comes with an adhesive heatsink. It sticks to the IC's plastic body, so it helps only a little.
The built-in voltmeter (±0.1 V) runs from an LM317. Near the thermal limit, especially at high VIN, it can shut down and the display goes blank while the converter keeps working.
The left button turns the display on or off. The right button switches it between Vin and Vout, shown by the IN/OUT LEDs. A green LED lights when power is applied.
Output ripple and noise are typically 50-200 mV peak-to-peak. Switching frequency is 180 kHz (190 kHz measured).
Four corner mounting holes, with standoffs included.
Wire the input and output before applying power. Components get hot under heavy load.

components.name: OV2640 2MP DVP camera module
components.description: The classic 2 MP camera of the ESP32-CAM. On-chip JPEG lets an ESP32 or STM32 (DCMI) grab and stream frames over Wi-Fi with little processing. Sold as cheap 24-pin FPC modules with many lens angles.

variants.note: Arducam Mini CCM, 52° lens, 650 nm IR-cut, 24-pin gold-finger FPC

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: On-chip JPEG makes it usable on an ESP32 without PSRAM-heavy processing; raw RGB565 above QVGA needs PSRAM.
Max frame rates: UXGA 15 fps, SVGA 30 fps, CIF 60 fps.
24-pin 0.5 mm FPC pinouts differ between vendors. Check the module against your board's socket (ESP32-CAM style is the most common).
Seeed has discontinued its OV2640 module in favour of the OV3660/OV5640. For new designs, consider those or the GC2145.

components.name: OV3660 3MP DVP camera module
components.description: A 3 MP BSI sensor with on-chip JPEG that drops into OV2640 sockets on ESP32-CAM-style boards. Gives sharper frames and 60 fps at VGA for MCU vision projects.

variants.note: IADIY module, 120° M7 lens, 21 or 75 mm FPC (body = camera head)

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Pin-compatible with OV2640 24-pin modules, but it has a different register map and needs driver support.
Max frame rates: 2048×1536 15 fps, 1080p 20 fps, 720p 45 fps, VGA 60 fps, QVGA 120 fps.
Shipped on newer XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense boards in place of the OV2640. No autofocus.

components.name: OV5640 5MP DVP/MIPI camera module
components.description: A 5 MP sensor with on-chip JPEG, a VCM autofocus driver and both DVP and 2-lane MIPI outputs. It's the high-end choice for ESP32-S3, STM32 DCMI and RP2040 cameras, and it does 90 fps at VGA.

variants.note: Adafruit breakout, 72° autofocus lens, 2×9 0.1" header, onboard 24 MHz clock

notes: Max frame rates: 2592×1944 15 fps, 1080p 30 fps, 720p 60 fps, VGA 90 fps, QVGA 120 fps.
Autofocus only works on modules with a VCM lens. The AF firmware is loaded over I²C at start-up.
Runs warm, so give it heat-sinking (the Adafruit breakout has a thermal pad). OmniVision recommends MIPI for high-resolution YUV.
Full 5 MP frames on an ESP32-S3 need PSRAM even with JPEG.

components.name: OV7670 VGA DVP camera module

Pinouts differ between 18-pin header versions (some have RESET/PWDN). Check before wiring.

components.name: GC0308 VGA DVP camera module

components.name: GC2145 2MP DVP/MIPI camera module

components.name: Himax HM0360 low-power VGA mono camera

Image pipelines run at about 40 fps at QVGA and below. Full 5 MP stills are possible.
Takes 4.7–5.7 V on VIN and draws about 130 mA active. I/O is 3.3 V and not 5 V tolerant. Swappable sensor modules include global-shutter and thermal.

components.name: Seeed Grove Vision AI Module V2
components.description: A low-cost TinyML vision board with a Himax WiseEye2 HX6538 (dual Cortex-M55 + Ethos-U55 NPU) and a CSI port for an OV5647 camera. Runs YOLO/MobileNet models and reports results to an MCU over I²C (Grove) or UART.

variants.note: Board only, camera sold separately (e.g. OV5647-62, $7.90). XIAO 2×7 header plus Grove I²C and USB-C

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Needs a Raspberry Pi-style OV5647 CSI camera. The resolution, fps and 62° FOV here are for the OV5647-62 camera, and inference runs on downscaled frames.
Models are deployed with SenseCraft AI (TensorFlow/PyTorch, YOLOv5/v8, MobileNet). Has up to 2432 KB of system memory, a PDM microphone and an SD slot.
Runs on 5 V. The board size is measured from Seeed's dimension drawing (about 40×20 mm including USB-C).

components.name: Arducam OV9281 1MP Global Shutter USB Camera
components.description: A plug-and-play UVC webcam board with a 1 MP mono global-shutter OV9281 that streams 100 fps MJPEG at 1280×800. Good for fiducial tracking and visual odometry on a Pi, Jetson or PC.

variants.note: USB 2.0 UVC with 1 m cable, low-distortion M12 lens (70° horizontal), no IR-cut

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Needs a USB host such as a Raspberry Pi, Jetson or PC (UVC, no driver needed). It can't connect directly to an MCU camera port.
100 fps is MJPEG only. Uncompressed YUY2 runs at 10 fps.
5 V USB power, 200 mA max.

components.name: MCP73831
components.description: Tiny 500 mA linear charger for one Li-ion/LiPo cell from USB, with a single tri-state STAT pin; the classic choice for small boards.

variants.note: 4.20 V, 2x3 mm DFN with exposed pad (better thermals)

notes: No battery protection: use a protected cell or add DW01A + FS8205A.
STAT is tri-state (high/low/Hi-Z), so it can drive two LEDs or one MCU pin.
Charge current = 1000 V / RPROG; keep it ≤ 1C of the cell.
SOT-23 heats up at 500 mA from 5 V: give it copper.

components.name: TP4056
components.description: Ultra-cheap 1 A linear charger for one Li-ion cell in ESOP-8, with CHRG/STDBY LED outputs and an NTC input; the chip on most blue USB charger boards.
notes: No battery protection: pair with DW01A + FS8205A (like the common 03962A module).
Linear: at 1 A from 5 V it burns ~1 W and folds back without a large ground pad.
Ground TEMP to disable the NTC check.
Abs max VCC is 8 V.

components.name: TP4057
components.description: 500 mA linear Li-ion charger in SOT-23-6 with battery reverse-polarity protection and two open-drain status pins (CHRG, STDBY).
notes: SOT-23 gets thermally limited above ~400 mA; a 0.5–1 Ω series resistor on VCC spreads the heat.
No NTC input and no battery protection.
Abs max VCC is 9 V.

components.name: BQ21040
components.description: 0.8 A linear charger for one 4.2 V Li-ion cell in SOT-23-6, 30 V input rating with 6.6 V OVP, NTC input and a CHG status pin.
notes: Fixed 4.2 V and a fixed 10 h safety timer.
Rated 0 to 125 °C junction (not -40 °C).

components.name: BQ24074
components.description: 1.5 A linear Li-ion charger with power path: OUT runs the system from USB/DC while the battery charges, with selectable 100/500 mA USB limits and VIN-DPM.
notes: EN1/EN2 select USB100, USB500 or the ILIM-resistor limit (up to 1.5 A).
VIN-DPM holds the input at ~4.5 V in USB modes, so a 6 V panel won't collapse (Adafruit's solar charger uses this).
OUT is regulated to 4.4 V max: safe for 3.3 V LDOs.

components.name: MCP73871
components.description: 1 A linear Li-ion charger with load sharing (power path), USB 100/500 mA selection, VPCC input-voltage regulation for solar, and STAT1/STAT2/PG outputs.

variants.note: 4.20 V, 6 h timer, LBO 3.1 V, tape & reel
4.20 V, 6 h timer, LBO 3.1 V, tube

notes: 1.8 A max total input (system + charge).
Also has a low-battery output (LBO) on -xCC options.
Used on Adafruit's PowerBoost 1000C and older USB/DC/Solar charger.

components.name: BQ25170
components.description: 800 mA linear charger for one Li-ion or LiFePO4 cell in a 2x2 mm WSON; a VSET resistor picks 3.5–3.7 V (LiFePO4) or 4.05–4.4 V (Li-ion).
notes: 30 V tolerant input with 6.6 V OVP.
VSET resistor outside 18–100 kΩ suspends charging.
No official KiCad symbol: pin table is hand-made from the datasheet.

components.name: BQ25172
components.description: 800 mA linear charger for 1–6 series NiMH cells in a 2x2 mm WSON: cell count by VSET resistor, timer-based termination, NTC input and a STAT pin.
notes: Constant-current only; ends charge on the TMR timer (4–22 h) or OUT OVP, no -ΔV detection.
No official KiCad symbol: pin table is hand-made from the datasheet.

components.name: CN3058E
components.description: Low-cost 1 A linear charger for one LiFePO4 cell (3.6 V, adjustable up with a resistor) with CHRG/DONE outputs and an NTC input, in ESOP-8.
notes: LiFePO4 only (3.6 V); FB pin allows Kelvin sensing at the cell.
Abs max on all pins is 6.5 V: no input OVP.
Solder the exposed pad to ground for full current.

components.name: BQ25895
components.description: I²C 5 A buck charger for one Li-ion cell with NVDC power path, BC1.2 D+/D- detection, 3.1 A 5 V boost (OTG), ADC and up to 14 V input.
notes: Starts in autonomous mode with safe defaults; the watchdog reverts settings if the host stops writing.
INT pin pulses on status changes.
VINDPM (up to 15.3 V) lets it hold a panel near its MPP.

components.name: BQ25601
components.description: I²C 3 A buck charger for one Li-ion cell with NVDC power path, 1.2 A USB OTG boost, PSEL USB/adapter input select and STAT/PG outputs.
notes: No D+/D- pins: PSEL picks 500 mA (USB) or 2.4 A (adapter) until the host programs IINDPM.
VINDPM only goes to 5.4 V, so it isn't meant for 9–12 V solar panels.

components.name: BQ25798
components.description: I²C 5 A buck-boost charger for 1–4 series Li-ion/LiFePO4 cells from 3.6–24 V (USB-PD), with solar MPPT, dual-input mux, OTG up to 22 V and NVDC power path.

variants.note: VQFN-HR (hot-rod) package, no single exposed pad

notes: Cell count and charge voltage come from the PROG resistor at power-up, then I²C.
Hot-rod VQFN: copy TI's layout for the power pins.
Good fit for 2S–4S robot packs charged from USB-C PD or a panel.

components.name: BQ25887
components.description: I²C 2 A boost charger that charges a 2S Li-ion pack from 5 V USB, with integrated cell balancing, 16-bit ADC, NTC input and STAT/PG outputs.
notes: No power path and no OTG: the system runs from the pack.
Input is USB only (6.2 V max operating, 20 V abs max).
PSEL selects a 500 mA (USB) or 3 A (adapter) input limit before I²C setup.

components.name: BQ24650
components.description: Standalone synchronous buck charge controller for solar: input-voltage-regulation MPPT, 5–28 V panel, 1–6 cell Li-ion, LiFePO4 or lead-acid, up to 10 A.
notes: Controller: needs two external NMOS FETs, inductor and sense resistor (charge current = 40 mV / Rsense).
MPPT is a fixed input-voltage setpoint (MPPSET divider), not perturb-and-observe.
Float voltage set by a resistor divider on VFB.

components.name: CN3791
components.description: Cheap 4 A PWM buck charge controller for one 4.2 V Li-ion cell from a 4.5–28 V solar panel, with constant-voltage MPPT and CHRG/DONE outputs.
notes: Controller: needs an external P-MOSFET, Schottky diode, inductor and sense resistor (120 mV / RCS).
MPPT pin regulates the panel voltage via a divider (1.205 V reference).
No NTC input; fixed 4.2 V.

components.name: BQ25504
components.description: Nano-power boost charger for energy harvesting: cold-starts at 600 mV, harvests down to 130 mV from small solar cells or TEGs with MPPT, into a Li-ion cell or supercap.
notes: For µW–mW sources: charge current is only ~100 mA max.
Battery OV/UV and VBAT_OK thresholds are set with 10 MΩ resistor dividers.
330 nA quiescent current.

components.name: IP2312
components.description: 5 V input, 3 A synchronous buck charger for one Li-ion cell in ESOP-8 with NTC protection, two LED status drivers and adaptive input current.

variants.note: IP2312U; battery voltage (4.2/4.3/4.35/4.4 V) set by a resistor on D1

notes: 5 V input only (OVP at 5.6 V).
ICHG open = 2.1 A; with a resistor ICC = 135000 / RICHG (0.8–3 A).
Needs a 1 µH inductor; datasheets are in Chinese.

components.name: IP2326
components.description: 15 W boost charger for 2S or 3S Li-ion packs from a 5 V (or QC fast-charge) USB input, with 2S cell balancing, NTC input and status/LED outputs, in QFN-24.
notes: CON_SEL open = 2S, 1 kΩ to GND = 3S.
DP/DM request a higher fast-charge input voltage from QC adapters.
No power path: the robot runs from the pack.

components.name: IP5306
components.description: Power-bank SoC in ESOP-8: 2.1 A switching Li-ion charger plus 5 V 2.1 A boost output with one inductor, 4-LED fuel gauge and a power key.
notes: The boost shuts off after 32 s below ~45 mA load: an MCU in sleep can lose power (the IP5306-I2C variant can disable this).
LED1–3 are charlieplexed fuel-gauge LED drivers, not logic outputs.
Rated 0–70 °C ambient.

components.name: BQ25713
components.description: I²C NVDC buck-boost charge controller for 1–4S packs from 3.5–24 V (USB-C PD), up to 8.1 A charge, OTG output 3–20.8 V and system power monitor.
notes: Controller: four external NMOS FETs, inductor and sense resistors; charge starts at 0 A until the host writes ChargeCurrent().
No TS/NTC pin: monitor battery temperature with the MCU.
Pin-compatible with BQ25703A; BQ25713B is the variant with different defaults.

components.name: Adafruit Universal USB/DC/Solar LiPo Charger (BQ24074)
components.description: BQ24074 breakout with USB-C, DC jack and JST ports: charges one LiPo at up to 1.5 A from 5–10 V USB, DC or a 6 V solar panel, with a load-sharing output.

variants.note: 1 A default; 0.5 / 1.5 A by solder jumper

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Linear: anything above ~6 V input is lost as heat, so use 6–7 V panels.
LOAD output never exceeds 4.4 V.
PGOOD and CHG are open-drain pins on the header; no DONE LED.

components.name: Adafruit PowerBoost 1000C
components.description: MCP73871 load-sharing LiPo charger (1 A from micro-USB) plus a TPS61090 5.2 V boost for 1 A+ output, with enable and low-battery pins: a small UPS for 5 V projects.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: A battery must always be connected.
CHG/DONE are LEDs only; LBO (low battery <3.2 V) is pulled up to VBAT, not 3.3 V-safe.
Size given with the USB-A jack fitted.

components.name: Adafruit Micro-Lipo Charger (USB-C)
components.description: Tiny MCP73831 LiPo charger with a USB-C jack and JST-PH battery plug: 100 mA by default, 500 mA with a solder jumper, red/green charge LEDs.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: No power path: the load sits directly on the battery.
Status is on LEDs only, not broken out to a pad.

components.name: DFRobot Solar Power Manager 5V
components.description: Solar/USB charger board for one Li-ion cell (CN3165, 900 mA, constant-voltage MPPT for 5–6 V panels) with a 5 V 1 A boosted output and battery protection.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Solar input is 4.5–6 V only: use a 5 V/6 V panel.
EN pin switches the 5 V output from an MCU GPIO.
Battery OV/UV/OC and reverse-polarity protection on board.

components.name: SparkFun LiPo Charger Plus
components.description: USB-C single-cell LiPo charger board using the MCP73833: up to 1 A, selectable charge rate, optional NTC thermistor, charge/power/done LEDs and two JST ports.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: No power path: the load shares the battery.
Status is on LEDs only.

components.name: TCAN1042HV
components.description: TI ±70 V fault-protected CAN FD transceiver with a VIO pin for 3.3 V MCUs and standby with remote wake. A robust pick for CAN/CAN FD links to motor controllers on 24-48 V robot power buses.

variants.note: G grade: 5 Mbit/s CAN FD, VIO pin
rated 2 Mbit/s CAN FD, VIO pin

notes: 5 V VCC; VIO (3.0-5.5 V) sets the TXD/STB/RXD levels, so it talks directly to 3.3 V MCUs
Only the G parts (TCAN1042HGVDR) are rated 5 Mbit/s; TCAN1042HVDR is rated 2 Mbit/s
STB high = low-power standby with remote wake-up; tie it low for normal mode
Same pinout as the TJA1042T/3
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: TJA1051T/3
components.description: Very common, cheap CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s) with a VIO pin for 3.3 V MCUs. The default PHY for motor-controller CAN buses (ODrive-style drives, robot joints) when no sleep/wake is needed.

variants.note: HVSON8 3x3 mm with exposed pad, VIO pin

notes: 5 V VCC; VIO (2.8-5.5 V, /3 variants only) for direct 3.3 V MCU connection
No standby/wake: pin 8 (S) selects silent (listen-only) mode; tie low for normal operation
AEC-Q100, ±58 V on CANH/CANL
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: TJA1042T/3
components.description: CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s) with VIO for 3.3 V MCUs and a very-low-current standby with bus wake-up. Good for battery-powered robots whose CAN nodes need to sleep.

variants.note: HVSON8 3x3 mm with exposed pad, VIO pin

notes: 5 V VCC; VIO (2.8-5.5 V) on the /3 variants only; on TJA1042T (no /3) pin 5 is SPLIT
STB high = standby (about 10 µA) with bus wake-up reported on RXD; tie low for normal mode
AEC-Q100, ±58 V on CANH/CANL
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: TJA1443
components.description: CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s) with sleep mode: battery-powered wake receiver, INH output to switch the node's regulator, WAKE pin and ERR_N diagnostics. For robots that power down whole nodes and wake them over CAN.
notes: Three supplies: VBAT 4.5-28 V (wake logic), VCC 4.5-5.5 V (transmitter), VIO 2.95-5.5 V (logic)
INH switches an external regulator off in sleep; wakes from the bus, the WAKE pin or the host
Drop-in replacement for the TJA1043
Bus pins rated -36/+40 V, not ±58 V
EN and STB_N select the mode; tie both high for normal mode if you don't need sleep

components.name: MCP2562FD
components.description: CAN FD transceiver with a 1.8-5.5 V VIO pin and 5 µA standby with bus wake. Works straight from 1.8/3.3 V MCUs; a common pick for CAN FD links to motor drivers and sensor nodes.
notes: 5 V VDD; VIO 1.8-5.5 V
Marketed for 2/5/8 Mbit/s but only 5 Mbit/s is guaranteed in the datasheet
STBY high = standby with wake-up on RXD; tie low for normal mode
MCP2561FD is the same die with SPLIT instead of VIO on pin 5
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: MCP2542FD
components.description: CAN FD transceiver specified up to 8 Mbit/s, with a 1.7-5.5 V VIO for low-voltage MCUs and 4 µA standby with wake on CAN activity. Suits fast CAN FD buses to motor drivers and sensor hubs.
notes: 5 V VDD; VIO 1.7-5.5 V
Bit time down to 125 ns (8 Mbit/s); the 8 Mbit/s loop-delay symmetry is characterized only
STBY high = standby; MCP2542FD wakes on any CAN activity, MCP2542WFD only on the ISO 11898-2:2016 wake-up pattern
AEC-Q100, ±58 V bus
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: CA-IF1042LVS
components.description: Low-cost Chipanalog CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s), pin-compatible with the TCAN1042V, with VIO for 3.3 V MCUs and standby with remote wake. A budget second source for CAN FD motor-controller buses.
notes: 'LVS' = ±42 V family, VIO on pin 5, SOIC-8; CA-IF1042LS has NC on pin 5
5 V VCC; VIO 3.0-5.5 V; STB high = standby with remote wake
Bus fault only ±42 V (±6 kV HBM), lower than the TI/NXP parts
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: SIT1042AT/3
components.description: Low-cost TJA1042T/3-compatible CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s) with VIO for 3.3 V MCUs, ±70 V bus protection and standby with bus wake-up. A cheap, well-stocked option for CAN FD robot buses.

variants.note: DFN-8 3x3 mm with exposed pad, VIO pin

notes: Pin-compatible with the NXP TJA1042T/3 (TXD, GND, VCC, RXD, VIO, CANL, CANH, STB)
A-revision of the SIT1042 (better symmetry, lower emissions); the old SIT1042T/3 is hard to find
5 V VCC; VIO for 3-5 V MCUs; STB high = standby with remote wake
SIT1051AT/3 is the silent-mode (no standby) sibling, like the TJA1051
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: SN65HVD230
components.description: Cheap 3.3 V classic CAN transceiver (1 Mbit/s) in SOIC-8, a direct match for 3.3 V MCUs with a CAN peripheral (STM32 bxCAN, ESP32 TWAI). Fine for CAN 2.0 links to hobby motor controllers. Not CAN FD.
notes: Single 3.0-3.6 V supply; logic levels follow VCC
Rs pin 8: GND = full speed, resistor to GND = slope control, high = standby
Standby is listen-only (driver off, receiver on, 370 µA): the MCU watches RXD and pulls Rs low to transmit
Bus pins rated only -4..+16 V abs max: a short to 24 V will kill it. Common-mode range -2..+7 V
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: MCP2551
components.description: Classic 5 V CAN 2.0 transceiver (1 Mbit/s, ±42 V bus pins) found in many older robot and hobby CAN designs. Not recommended for new designs: use the MCP2561/MCP2562FD instead.
notes: NRND since datasheet rev G (2016); Microchip points to the MCP2561
5 V only: TXD accepts 3.3 V logic, but RXD swings to VDD, so a 3.3 V MCU needs a divider or a 5 V-tolerant pin
RS pin: GND = high speed, resistor = slope control, high = standby (receiver monitors the bus; the first message may be lost)
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: ISO1042
components.description: 5 kVrms isolated CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s, ±70 V bus fault, ±30 V common mode). Breaks ground loops on CAN FD links to motor drives and battery packs. Needs an isolated 5 V supply on the bus side.

variants.note: 8-pin wide-body SOIC (DWV), 8.5 mm creepage, basic isolation, -40..125 °C

notes: Bus side VCC2 (4.5-5.5 V) needs its own isolated 5 V supply (isolated DC-DC module or transformer driver)
Logic side VCC1 runs at 1.71-1.89 V or 2.25-5.5 V, so 1.8/3.3/5 V MCUs connect directly
No standby or silent pin
Not pin-compatible with the ISO1044
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: ISO1044
components.description: Low-cost 3 kVrms isolated CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s, ±58 V bus fault) in a plain narrow SOIC-8. A compact way to isolate a CAN FD link to motor controllers. Needs an isolated 5 V supply on the bus side.
notes: Bus side VCC2 (4.5-5.5 V) needs an isolated 5 V supply; VCC1 takes 1.71-1.89 V or 2.25-5.5 V logic
Narrow body: 3 kVrms basic isolation, less creepage than the wide-body ISO1042
Common-mode range only ±12 V (ISO1042: ±30 V)
No standby or silent pin
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: ISOW1044
components.description: 5 kVrms isolated CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s, ±58 V) with a built-in isolated DC-DC, a spare isolated GPIO and standby with bus wake-up. A one-chip isolated CAN FD node for motor drives on a 5 V rail.

variants.note: 20-pin DFM (SOIC-20 wide footprint, 3.55 mm tall), basic isolation, -40..125 °C

notes: VDD 4.5-5.5 V powers the DC-DC; VIO runs at 1.71-1.89 V or 2.25-5.5 V
Some pins must be joined on the PCB: GNDIO to GND1, VISOOUT to VSIN/VISOIN, GND2 to GISOIN
STB high or floating = standby with WUP remote wake; tie STB low for normal mode
About 20 mA of spare isolated output for bus-side circuits
Often out of stock at distributors; TI suggests the ISOW1050 as an alternative
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: ADM3053
components.description: Isolated classic CAN transceiver with a built-in isoPower DC-DC (2.5 kVrms, 1 Mbit/s): one 5 V rail powers both sides, no separate isolated supply. Good for CANopen nodes on robot arms. Not CAN FD.
notes: Single 5 V VCC feeds the internal isolated DC-DC; VIO (3.0-5.5 V) sets the MCU logic level
isoPower switches at high frequency: follow ADI AN-0971 layout guidance for radiated emissions
RS pin must not float: GND = full speed, resistor = slope control, high = standby
Classic CAN only, -40..85 °C
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: MCP2515
components.description: Classic CAN 2.0B controller on SPI (1 Mbit/s, 3 TX / 2 RX buffers, 6 filters). Needs an external CAN transceiver. Adds a CAN port to MCUs or SBCs without one, for legacy CAN motor drivers and sensors.

variants.note: TSSOP-20, -40..85 °C; pins 6 and 15 are NC, so numbering differs from the SOIC

notes: Controller only: pair it with a CAN transceiver (TXCAN/RXCAN go to the transceiver's TXD/RXD)
SPI up to 10 MHz, modes 0,0 and 1,1
Oscillator max 40 MHz only at VDD 4.5-5.5 V; 25 MHz max over 2.7-5.5 V
Sleep mode wakes on CAN bus activity (WAKIF) and comes back in Listen-Only mode: the MCU must set the mode again
Classic CAN only: no CAN FD frames

components.name: MCP2518FD
components.description: CAN FD controller on SPI (1 Mbit/s arbitration, 8 Mbit/s data, 31 FIFOs, 32 filters). Pair it with a CAN FD transceiver to add a CAN FD motor or sensor bus to any MCU or SBC.

variants.note: VDFN-14 3x4.5 mm with EP (to VSS) and wettable flanks, -40..125 °C, tape & reel

notes: Controller only: needs an external CAN FD transceiver
SPI: 20 MHz in the headline, but the AC table limits SCK to 17 MHz
Needs a 40, 20 or 4 MHz crystal or clock; use 40 MHz for 8 Mbit/s CAN FD
INT0/GPIO0 can work as XSTBY and drive the transceiver's standby pin
Sleep mode wakes on RXCAN activity or nCS

components.name: MCP251863
components.description: MCP2518FD CAN FD controller plus ATA6563 transceiver in one package, SPI to the host, 5 Mbit/s data phase. A one-chip CAN FD port to motor controllers from a 3.3 V MCU (the transceiver needs 5 V).

variants.note: VQFN-28 5x5 mm, wettable flanks, -40..125 °C, tape & reel

notes: Three supplies: transceiver VCC 4.5-5.5 V, VIO 2.8-5.5 V, controller VDD 2.7-5.5 V
Controller TXCAN/RXCAN and transceiver TXD/RXD are separate pins: wire them together on the PCB
STBY has an internal pull-up, so the part stays in standby until STBY is pulled low
Bus pins rated -27..+42 V DC (asymmetric)
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: TCAN4550
components.description: Bosch M_CAN CAN FD controller and transceiver in one package, on SPI (18 MHz), with a 5 V LDO, WAKE pin and INH. Runs straight off a 12/24 V battery to give any MCU a CAN FD motor or sensor bus.
notes: VSUP must be 6-24 V and cannot run from a 5 V rail alone. The internal LDO makes the 5 V VCCOUT for the transceiver
VIO sets the 3.3 or 5 V logic level
Needs a 20 or 40 MHz crystal or clock on OSC1
Starts in standby and drops to sleep after about 4 min (tINACTIVE) unless the MCU services it
TI recommends the TCAN4550-Q1 as the drop-in upgrade

components.name: TCAN4550-Q1
components.description: Automotive TCAN4550: M_CAN CAN FD controller, transceiver and 5 V/70 mA LDO on SPI, 8 Mbit/s, ±58 V bus. Pin-compatible upgrade of the TCAN4550 for 12/24 V robot CAN FD buses.

variants.note: VQFN-20 3.5x4.5 mm, EP to GND, AEC-Q100 Grade 1

notes: Pin-compatible with the TCAN4550, with wider VSUP (5.5-30 V), ±58 V bus and 8 Mbit/s
VCCOUT 5 V LDO can supply up to 70 mA to external loads
Needs a 20 or 40 MHz crystal or clock; same tINACTIVE fail-safe as the TCAN4550
Costs about the same as the industrial TCAN4550 at LCSC

components.name: MAX3485
components.description: 3.3 V half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver, 10 Mbit/s, 32 nodes, standard 75176 pinout in SOIC-8. The classic way to put a 3.3 V MCU UART on a Modbus RTU or smart-servo bus.
notes: One GPIO drives DE and /RE together for direction
A/B rated -7.5..+12.5 V abs max; no ESD rating in the datasheet (the MAX3485E is the ±15 kV version): add a TVS on field wiring
Shutdown (/RE high, DE low) but no bus wake-up
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: SP3485
components.description: Very cheap 3.3 V half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver, 10 Mbit/s, 32 nodes, 75176 pinout. A JLCPCB basic-style part for Modbus sensors, RS-485 servo buses and robot sub-networks.
notes: 3.3 V ±5% supply; logic inputs tolerate up to 6 V
Only ±2 kV HBM ESD: add a TVS (e.g. SM712) on A/B for off-board cables
Receiver fail-safe: output high for open or shorted inputs
Needs 120 Ω termination at both bus ends

components.name: THVD1450

components.name: MAX485

components.name: MAX13487E

components.name: TJA1021

components.name: LAN8720A

components.name: LAN9252

components.name: VL53L0X
components.description: Classic single-zone ToF ranger: up to 2 m (1.2 m in default mode) with a 25° cone over I²C. Cheap and well supported by Arduino/Pololu/Adafruit libraries for robot obstacle detection; the VL53L1X/L4CX reach further.

currentMa = 19 mA active-ranging average including the VCSEL (33 ms budget). Peaks reach 40 mA

components.name: VL53L1X

Accuracy is ST's ranging error (accuracy + repeatability), long mode at 100 ms: ±20 mm in the dark, ±25 mm in ambient light
Minimum ranging distance 4 cm. Closer targets are detected but not measured accurately

components.name: VL53L4CD

currentMa = 22 mA typ (24 max) active-ranging average including the VCSEL. Peaks reach 40 mA. Autonomous low-power mode wakes the host with a distance-threshold interrupt

components.name: VL6180X

components.name: TMF8820
components.description: 3x3-zone direct ToF (1 cm to 5 m) with a wide adjustable FoV (up to 63° diagonal) and up to two objects per zone, in a 4.6 x 2.0 mm OLGA module. Cheap wide-angle obstacle and presence sensing for robots over I²C.
notes: Boots into a ROM bootloader: the host must download the ams measurement firmware (in the TMF882x driver package) into RAM over I²C after every power-up or EN low (~50 ms at 1 MHz I²C), then write the calibration data for the SPAD map in use.
FoV fields are the 3x3 wide mode, 41°x52° (63° diagonal). The default SPAD map is 3x3 at 33°x32° (45° diagonal).
Range: 5 m on 90% white (all zones) and 4-5 m on 18% grey under 350 lux LED light (3x3, 33°x32°, 30 Hz). Centre zone drops to 1 m on white at 10 klux sunlight-equivalent.
Accuracy ±3% at >=333 mm, ±10-19 mm closer. Reports the closest and second-closest object per zone, with a confidence (SNR) value.
VDD 2.7-3.5 V (3.0 V typ). I²C/INT pull-ups 1.62-3.5 V, up to 1 MHz, default address 0x41, I3C-tolerant.
141 mW average (about 47 mA at 3 V) in default 3x3 mode at 30 Hz; 57 mA while the VCSEL is ranging; 19 mW in low-power 50 k-iteration mode; 2 µA with EN low. Operating range -40 to 85 °C.

components.name: TMF8821
components.description: Configurable 3x3, 4x4 or 3x6-zone direct ToF (1 cm to 5 m, up to 63° diagonal FoV) in a 4.6 x 2.0 mm OLGA module. Wide-angle obstacle mapping and gap finding for small robots over I²C.
notes: zones = 18: the 3x6 mode (33°x60° FoV) gives 18 zones, which ams lists as the maximum. The 4x4 mode gives 16 zones at 41°x52° (63° diagonal); the FoV fields are that mode.

Range in 4x4 mode, 90% white, 350 lux LED: 5 m centre zones but only 2.9-3 m edge and corner zones; 18% grey 4 m centre, 1.4-1.5 m edge. Centre zone 1 m at 10 klux sunlight-equivalent.

components.name: TMF8828

components.name: AFBR-S50MV85G
components.description: 32-pixel indirect ToF module (850 nm) for 10 m+ ranging at up to 3 kHz frame rate, usable in 100-200 klx sunlight. Fast 1D/3D distance and motion sensing for outdoor robots; needs a Cortex-M host running Broadcom's driver over SPI.

variants.note: Through-hole module, 4.3 mm pins; wave soldering only (no reflow, no wash). Tubes of 60.

notes: No device mapping: it is SPI-only and needs Broadcom's driver library on a Cortex-M host, so it does not fit the I²C multizone ToF device.

No processor on the module: an Arm Cortex-M host must run Broadcom's precompiled ToF driver library (API/SDK, github.com/Broadcom/AFBR-S50-API). It needs SPI (pins also usable as GPIO for EEPROM bit-banging), one IRQ GPIO and a dedicated hardware timer for eye-safety timing.
Interface is SPI only (3.3 V CMOS, up to 25 MHz), not I²C. Supply 5 V (4.5-5.5 V; 4.75-5.25 V for the full temperature range).

Range up to 10 m on 8% black indoors; under 7 m on 8% black at 100 klx sunlight; further on bright targets in dual-frequency mode (<=100 Hz). Unambiguous range 50 m (short-range mode) or 100 m (long-range mode) with dual frequency.
32 pixels (8x4 hexagonal, 1.55° each); receiver FoV 12.4°x5.4°, but the 4°x4° laser beam lights only about 7 (5-16) pixels at a time.
Frame rate: 25 Hz is the datasheet's default reference rate; up to 1 kHz with all pixels, 2 kHz with 16 and 3 kHz with 8 pixels (needs SPI >=12-21 MHz).
Accuracy ±1% relative, ±10 mm zero-point offset. Precision ~10 mm typ (8% target at 4 m, 25 Hz).
33 mA typical (32 mA sensor + ~1 mA laser), 165 mW active. Operating range -20 to 70 °C.
Laser Class 1 only with Broadcom's software configuration and design rules; otherwise it must be treated as Class 3B.
Ambient: 100 klx typ, 200 klx max (on a 45% target). Startup/reset is specified up to 100 klx.

rateHz is the 11 Hz horizontal (azimuth) rotation and zones = 21,600 effective pts/s ÷ 11 Hz. Raw sampling is 43,200 pts/s and vertical mirror scan is 180 Hz. Point density is highest near the centre of the FOV
Built-in IMU (3-axis accelerometer + 3-axis gyro), sampled at 1 kHz and reported at 250 Hz
Power is 6 W at 25 °C on 12 V DC (≈500 mA). Unitree specifies a 12 V 1 A supply
Output is 3D position + 1D grayscale. Rated to 100 klux strong light, IP54, -10 to 60 °C. 905 nm with 25 W peak pulsed laser power, Class 1
The official store currently shows the L1 as unavailable. The L2 (Ethernet, 64,000 pts/s) is the successor

components.name: Unitree 4D LiDAR L2
components.description: Hemispherical 360°×96° 3D LiDAR (64,000 pts/s, 30 m, ≤2 cm) with Ethernet UDP and a built-in IMU, for SLAM, mapping and obstacle avoidance on legged and wheeled robots. It is the L1's successor.

variants.note: One-to-three pigtail with 9 live conductors: DC 3.5×1.35 power (2), RJ45 Ethernet (4 used: TX±, RX±) and GH1.25-4 serial plug (3 used: GND, RX, TX)

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Ethernet/USB to a computer; no MCU device mapping. The default output is ENET UDP (L2 at 192.168.1.62, sending from port 6101 to 192.168.1.2:6201). The alternative is 3.3 V TTL UART at 4,000,000 baud through the included USB Type-C adapter, but only one output can be active at a time
Range is 30 m @90% reflectivity and 15 m @10%. Near blind zone is 0.05 m (reference only)
FOV is 360°×90° in normal mode and 360°×96° in NEGA mode (the factory default). Range is slightly shorter in the extra 6°. A 2D mode gives a 180°/192° line at the same 64,000 pts/s

rateHz is the 5.55 Hz horizontal rotation and zones = 64,000 effective pts/s ÷ 5.55 Hz. Raw sampling is 128,000 pts/s and vertical scan is 216 Hz. Angular resolution is 0.64° and distance resolution 4.5 mm
Built-in IMU (3-axis accelerometer + 3-axis gyro), sampled at 1 kHz and reported at 500 Hz. It is disabled by default
Power is 10 W at 25 °C on 12 V DC (≈830 mA), up to 13 W in self-heating mode when cold. No point cloud is output until it warms up
Rated to 100 klux strong light, IP54, -10 to 50 °C, 905 nm Class 1

components.name: Livox Mid-360
components.description: Compact IP67 360°×59° 3D LiDAR (200k pts/s, 40 m @10% / 70 m @80%, 0.1 m blind zone) with a built-in IMU, for SLAM and obstacle avoidance on low-speed mobile robots, AGVs and quadrupeds.

variants.note: M12 A-code 12-pin male aviation connector: 2× power, 2× GND, 4× Ethernet, PPS in, GPS in, 2× reserved LVTTL out. The 1-to-3 splitter cable is sold separately

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Ethernet/USB to a computer; no MCU device mapping. Data goes over 100BASE-TX Ethernet (Livox SDK 2 / ROS driver). Time sync is IEEE 1588 PTPv2 or GPS (PPS + 9600-baud NMEA on 3.3 V LVTTL pins)
Range is 70 m @80% and 40 m @10% reflectivity, both specified at 100 klx ambient. Blind zone is 0.1 m, and 0.1–0.2 m data is reference only
FOV is 360° horizontal and -7° to +52° vertical (59°). Repetitive or non-repetitive scanning is switchable, and coverage builds up over longer integration times
rateHz is the 10 Hz typical frame rate and zones = 200,000 pts/s (first return) ÷ 10 Hz. Distance random error (1σ) is ≤2 cm @10 m. Angular random error is ≤0.15°
Built-in IMU (ICM40609, 3-axis accelerometer + gyro), pushed at 200 Hz
Power is 6.5 W at 25 °C on 9–27 V DC, ≈540 mA at the recommended 12 V. Start-up draws 18 W for ~8 s below 35 °C, and self-heating can reach 14 W at -20 to 0 °C
IP67, -20 to 55 °C, 905 nm Class 1. The SensorLidar price of $749 is sensor-only ($799 with the splitter cable). The DJI Store doesn't sell in every region
Livox distributors now ship the Mid-360S as the current version (same form factor, FOV and driver compatibility)
